text:
China’s, South Korea’s, and North Korea’s governments teach their citizens “false national histories.” This will be quite a long post, but I hope anyone interested in modern and contemporary East Asian history will read to the end.

Until just a few years ago, South Korean government and civic groups alike were spreading the claim, not only in Japan but around the world, that “more than 200,000 comfort women were forcibly taken.” The claim originated in a fantastical book by a Japanese fraudster named Yoshida Seiji(吉田清治). 

At the time, the Asahi Shimbun, a Japanese newspaper of high standing, used Yoshida’s book as the basis for vigorous attacks on the Japanese government. But about five years ago, it published a brief apology saying that “all of its articles concerning comfort women and Yoshida were false reports.”

Professor J. Mark Ramseyer of Harvard Law School in the United States published a peer-reviewed academic paper arguing that “the Japanese military had no need to forcibly take 200,000 women from the Korean Peninsula and make them comfort women.” To this day, no one has published a peer-reviewed academic paper refuting it. Nevertheless, if you ask various AI systems, they will confidently say that “the forced recruitment of 200,000 comfort women by the Japanese military is a fact.” 

At the time, Japanese people living on the Korean Peninsula made up less than 3 percent of the population. Most were teachers, government employees, or staff posted there by private companies. 
Naturally, Koreans served in the Korean police force; in some police stations, Japanese sergeants even served under Korean inspectors.

If the Japanese military really had abducted 200,000 Korean women by force, did Korean men—including Korean police officers at the time—simply stand by and watch?

The so-called Nanjing Massacre, as described by the Chinese Communist government, is also entirely fictitious. What the Japanese military was doing in Nanjing was fighting a war, and its adversary was the Chinese National Revolutionary Army. 

In the first place, the Japanese military and Japanese civilians had been legally stationed and living in China, just as U.S. forces and their families are currently stationed in Japan.

In addition to Japan, the great powers—including Britain, France, and the United States—initially stationed troops in China. 

These great powers stationed troops in China because, during the 1900 Boxer Rebellion, Chinese people behaved brutally toward foreign diplomats and failed to protect the safety of foreign nationals who held passports.

However, when the World War broke out in 1914, the great powers withdrew their troops from China to send them to the battlefields in Europe. In effect, the task of maintaining order in China was left to the Japanese military.

On May 5, 1923, a train robbery by Chinese bandits occurred near Lincheng, along the Tianjin–Pukou Railway(津浦鉄道) in Shandong Province.

The bandits abducted more than twenty foreigners—including women and children from Britain, the United States, France, Italy, Denmark, and Mexico—and another 300 passengers from an express train traveling from Pukou to Tianjin. 

They took them to a nearby mountain stronghold and demanded that the Chinese National Government incorporate them into its regular army, the National Revolutionary Army. 

In response, the government gave the bandits’ force of 2,000 men regular brigade status and guaranteed that it would not attack them, in order to secure the hostages’ release. In other words, the Chinese government turned terrorists into soldiers.

Among the hostages held in the mountain stronghold in Shandong was an American journalist (Theodore White). His book says the following:

    “When word spread that a large quantity of food had been obtained from the Red Cross, the bandits’ numbers swelled from 2,000 to around 3,000. Soldiers from warlord armies who had fallen on hard times and peasants looking for food joined the bandit group. A Chinese student who spoke English and had been taken hostage acted as an interpreter between the foreign hostages and the bandits. From the bandits’ whispered conversations, we learned that children from China who had been kidnapped were being held farther inland, beyond the stronghold where the bandits had gathered.  I along with a priest, actually found the place where they were being held. We entrusted a note about it to a Red Cross supply convoy, and the resulting newspaper story caused a great sensation.”

From the 1920s and ’30s—and, indeed, since ancient times—many Chinese soldiers had either been bandits or come from the ranks of coolies. Since China had no proper national conscription system, the parents of wealthy young men paid coolies to serve in their sons’ place. As a result, soldiers often behaved very badly. 

Even after becoming regular soldiers, they continued to plunder civilians, and it was commonplace for them to loot while on the move or stationed in an area during wartime. Even in peacetime, looting was sometimes tolerated when soldiers’ pay was delayed. In other words, soldiers and bandits were essentially the same people, joining or leaving whichever group offered them a better living. The Japanese government struggled with how to protect Japanese residents and law-abiding Chinese people from Chinese soldiers and bandits of this kind.

In 1927, the “real Nanjing Incident” took place. Consulates and other property belonging to Japan, Britain, the United States, and other countries in Nanjing were attacked by Chiang Kai-shek’s army during the Northern Expedition and by Nanjing residents who took advantage of the situation. The wife of the Japanese consul was gang-raped by more than ten Chinese soldiers, and everything in the consulate was looted. 

Warships from various countries were anchored in the Yangtze River. Britain and the United States retaliated with naval gunfire, but the Japanese government did not. The Chinese came to believe that “if the target is Japan, there will be no retaliation,” and attacked Japanese people all the more.

The conventional account says that the Sino-Japanese War began on July 7, 1937. That is not what actually happened. On that day, the Japanese military was conducting military exercises in an open field beneath the Marco Polo Bridge, near Beijing.

The exercise was a rehearsal for an inspection by senior officers at the regimental-commander level. The recruits, who had enlisted only a few months earlier, were to demonstrate that they could march in step and crawl forward while carrying rifles. That is why they were not wearing steel military helmets, and the ammunition in their rifles was blank. Live rounds were kept in sealed cardboard boxes and carried in their waist pouches; using them without authorization was a serious offense punishable by court-martial. 

The Chinese Revolutionary Army fired live ammunition at the Japanese troops during the exercise and provoked them. That is the truth of the matter. Agents of the Chinese Communist Party had infiltrated the Chinese Revolutionary Army.

A ceasefire agreement was concluded locally within a few days of the Marco Polo Bridge Incident, but the Chinese military repeatedly ignored it unilaterally and continued provoking the Japanese military.

On July 13, in the mǎcūn Incident(馬村事件), a Japanese infantry platoon came under fire from Chinese troops and suffered fatalities. 

In the Dahongmen Incident(大紅門事件), Chinese soldiers suddenly threw grenades into two Japanese army trucks, killing four Japanese soldiers. On July 14, Sergeant Ōgaki and Private Second Class Kondō were attacked by Chinese soldiers at Fengtai. Kondō was killed in a horrific manner: he was hit by six submachine-gun bullets and died instantly, his head was split in two with a Chinese saber, his brain was scattered, and his right leg was brutally severed.

The Langfang Incident was a battle between the Nationalist Army and the Japanese military at Langfang Station on July 25. On July 26, in the Guang’anmen Incident, Japanese soldiers were attacked at Guang’anmen in Beijing. Then, on July 29, the “Tongzhou Massacre(通州大虐殺)” took place. Read the post pinned to my profile for a full account of that incident. https://t.co/tmUgz5Yf4M
What did the Japanese government do after suffering all these losses?

Through Funatsu Tatsuichirō(船津辰一郎) , a businessman and former diplomat who enjoyed the trust of Chinese people and chaired the Cotton Spinners’ Association, the Japanese government approached Chiang Kai-shek’s side with a peace initiative. (The Funatsu Peace Initiative.)

Its terms were as follows. Japan would accept all of the Chinese Nationalist Party’s political demands on Japan:

1. Japan would make no compensation claim for the Tongzhou, Guang’anmen, or Langfang incidents, or for other attacks in which Chinese soldiers had killed Japanese people.

2. If the Chinese government wished to abrogate past agreements between Japan and China, Japan would be prepared to accept their cancellation. (This meant ending all such agreements, including the Tanggu Truce, the Dōihara–Qin Dechun Agreement, and the Umezu–He Yingqin Agreement.)

3. The East Hebei Anti-Communist Autonomous Government and the Hebei–Chahar Political Council would be dissolved, and their administrative authority transferred to Chiang Kai-shek’s central government.

4. Japanese forces increased after the Marco Polo Bridge Incident would be reduced to their pre-incident levels.

5. The East Hebei special-trade arrangement, which allowed low-tariff trade, would be ended, and the Chinese side would regain freedom to crack down on smuggling at sea.

6. The 1932 Shanghai Ceasefire Agreement would be terminated.

In return for Japan’s acceptance of the above, China was asked to agree to the following:

7. China would recognize Manchukuo, even if it did not do so publicly or in writing.

8. Japan and China would conclude an anti-Communist pact.

9. China must take thorough measures to crack down on anti-Japanese policies and anti-Japanese movements.

If that happened, the Nationalists would have no further reason to fight Japan. Japan was willing to make no compensation claim at all, even for the horrific Tongzhou Incident.

While these negotiations were under way, on August 9, Lieutenant Ōyama Isao(大山勇夫), commander of the Shanghai Special Naval Landing Force’s western detachment, and his driver, Seaman First Class Saitō Yozō, were shot and killed while traveling to inspect a Japanese cotton mill on the outskirts of Shanghai. After being shot with rifles, their bodies were mutilated and dismembered. Their intestines were pulled out, their genitals cut off, and their skulls smashed in half with a rifle butt. Their military sword, watch, shoes, and other belongings were looted.

In other words, Chiang Kai-shek’s Nationalist government in Nanking responded to peace negotiations by brutally murdering Navy Lieutenant Ōyama.

Before dawn on August 12, large units of Chiang Kai-shek’s regular army advanced to Shanghai and attacked the Japanese residential area of the Shanghai International Settlement, commonly known as the Shanghai concessions.

Even then, the Japanese side did not give up hope of a peaceful resolution. It convened a joint committee meeting with the great powers that had participated in the Shanghai Ceasefire Agreement and demanded that Chiang Kai-shek’s army withdraw. Representatives of the great powers recognized Japan’s good faith and urged the Chinese side to reconsider. China paid no attention, however, and launched an attack on the Japanese Naval Landing Force before dawn on August 13. Four thousand Japanese Naval Landing Force troops found themselves facing 200,000 of Chiang Kai-shek’s soldiers, and the Japanese government decided to send reinforcements from Japan. Thus began the Second Shanghai Incident. The Cabinet decided that the fighting that followed would be called the China Incident(支那事變).

On August 13, the Japanese Naval Landing Force limited itself to defensive tactics, taking into account that Shanghai was an international city and that the plenipotentiary representatives of the great powers had offered to mediate. It refrained from firing its antiaircraft guns even when Chinese military aircraft flew low over the International Settlement. Meanwhile, Chinese bombers dropped bombs that hit not only the Japanese district but also the French Concession. 

On that day, the Chinese air force tried to bomb Japanese naval vessels anchored in Shanghai, including the Izumo, but “accidentally” bombed the French Concession and Nanjing Road, damaging the Cathay Hotel, a department store, and other buildings. The dead and injured are said to have numbered more than 2,000. On August 23, China bombed two department stores in Shanghai as well, but spread propaganda around the world claiming that the Japanese military was responsible.

On the ground, the Japanese Naval Landing Force fought gun battles with Chinese soldiers who had changed into civilian clothes and disguised themselves as civilians. This conduct by the Chinese military constituted a serious violation of international law of war (the Hague Regulations on Land Warfare).

Let us imagine this situation in present-day Japan.

The U.S. military has bases in Japan, with its headquarters at Yokota Air Base, where American service members and their families live. 

Would it be justifiable for armed Japanese Self-Defense Forces to storm a U.S. military base and kill American service members simply because people were angry that the base existed in Japan? 

Would it be justifiable for Japanese civilians to suddenly throw stones at American service members eating in restaurants near a base, or stab them to death? 

That is what the Chinese did to Japanese soldiers and civilians in China from 1900 onward.

In September 1937, China accused Japan of repeatedly violating the International Red Cross Convention. Colonel Charles de Watteville of the International Committee of the Red Cross inspected Shanghai and Nanjing from late September until November. When he inspected a prisoner-of-war camp in Shanghai on October 13, he said he was “impressed by the Japanese military’s humane and fair conduct.”

During the Second Shanghai Incident, the Chinese military constructed pillboxes and other defensive positions in the neutral zone, in violation of the ceasefire agreement from the First Shanghai Incident, which prohibited either side from building military facilities in the neutral zone. It took the Japanese military two and a half months to break through the pillbox defenses, but Chiang Kai-shek’s army did not surrender; it retreated to the capital, Nanjing.

Along the way to Nanjing, Chiang Kai-shek’s army looted whatever it could. When there was nothing left to loot, it set fires and adopted a “scorched-earth” policy. Yet the conventional account attributes this to the Japanese military.

General Alexander von Falkenhausen, the German military adviser to Chiang Kai-shek’s army, proposed abandoning Nanjing, in light of the Japanese military’s advance toward the city. 

Chiang Kai-shek and the other senior officials of the Chinese National Government all agreed. Only General Tang Shengzhi(唐生智) volunteered, saying, “In that case, I will stake my life on defending Nanjing.” Chiang appointed him commander-in-chief of the Nanjing Defense Force, and the others left Nanjing by plane.

The Japanese military surrounded Nanjing and, on December 9, dropped large numbers of leaflets from aircraft carrying the following surrender demand:

    A million soldiers of the Japanese Army have already swept through the regions south of the Yangtze River. Nanjing is now surrounded. In view of the overall military situation, continuing the fighting will bring no benefit and only cause harm.

    Consider that Nanjing is the ancient capital of central China and the capital of the National Government. The tomb of the Ming dynasty’s Hongwu Emperor and the mausoleum of Sun Yat-sen are among the many historic sites there, and the city is a place of great beauty that embodies the cultural essence of East Asia.

    The Japanese Army will be extremely strict and show no mercy to those who resist. However, it will treat innocent civilians and Chinese troops who harbor no hostile intent with leniency, will not harm them, and is committed to protecting and preserving East Asian culture.

    If your forces continue fighting, Nanjing will inevitably be unable to escape the ravages of war. A thousand years of culture will be reduced to ashes, and ten years of effort will be brought to nothing.

    The commander-in-chief therefore, on behalf of the Japanese Army, urges your forces to open the gates of Nanjing peacefully and to take the following measures.

    Commander-in-Chief of the Imperial Japanese Army

    General Matsui Iwane

    Your response to this demand must be received by noon on December 10 at the sentry line on Zhongshan Road and Jurong Road.

    If your forces send a responsible representative authorized to act for the commander, arrangements can be made at that location with the Japanese commander’s representative to conclude the necessary agreement for the surrender of Nanjing.

    If no response is received by the appointed time, the Japanese Army will have no choice but to begin its assault on Nanjing.

The surrender demand from General Matsui Iwane, full of love for China, was rejected by Tang Shengzhi. That was the beginning of the assault on Nanjing. If the Chinese troops had raised a white flag and surrendered at that time, they would have qualified as prisoners of war. 

To be precise, a prisoner of war is a member of the armed forces who, in response to the enemy’s demand to surrender, raises a white flag, sends an envoy to the enemy to negotiate a ceasefire, and is taken captive after a ceasefire agreement has been reached and the soldier has disarmed. Lieutenant General Arthur Percival, who surrendered during the Malayan Campaign, is a good example.

The Japanese military captured Nanjing, but Tang Shengzhi had already fled the city with only a few of his closest subordinates. With no military command left, most of the Chinese soldiers did not surrender; instead, they tried to escape by climbing over the city walls, which were about ten meters high. They were trying to get away from the Chinese military system known since ancient times as the “Barrier troops(督戦隊)”: units stationed behind the lines that mercilessly shot soldiers who tried to leave their posts, surrender, or flee.

Near Yijiang Gate(挹江門), in the northwest of Nanjing, a gun battle took place between soldiers trying to escape to the port of Hsiakwan (Xiaguan), on the Yangtze River outside the city, and the Barrier troops. Soldiers who failed to escape outside the city hid their weapons, took off their uniforms, disguised themselves as civilians, and fled to the International Safety Zone, which was managed mainly by American missionaries.

The Japanese military detained Chinese men in the International Safety Zone who were suspected of being plainclothes soldiers(便衣兵). It determined whether they were civilians or Chinese soldiers by looking for tan lines left by military helmets, calluses and blisters on the trigger fingers of their right hands, and whether they wore underwear issued by the military.

As mentioned above, plainclothes soldiers in the Nanjing battle were not entitled to prisoner-of-war status and could be executed without a military trial. The Japanese military probably executed close to 20,000 plainclothes soldiers. But that was legal, and there is no grounds for condemnation.

The Chinese Communist Party’s definition of the so-called Nanjing Massacre is that “from December 13, 1937, for two months, the Japanese military committed atrocities and massacred 300,000 Chinese people, including women and children, inside Nanjing.”

Let us look at the burial records submitted at the Tokyo Trial concerning the bodies from the Battle of Nanjing.

The Red Swastika Society(紅卍字会), a charitable organization, reported that it had buried 1,793 bodies within the city of Nanjing. Of these, 34 were women and children—the only victims who could definitively be identified as civilians. Needless to say, those people were not massacred by the Japanese military; they were simply people who had been unable to escape the city or reach the International Safety Zone before Nanjing became a battlefield.

During the 100th session of the League of Nations Council—held from January 26 to February 2, 1938, approximately a month and a half after the fall of Nanking—the sixth meeting took place, beginning at noon on February 2, the representative of the Republic of China, Gu Weijun(顧維鈞), said that 20,000 people had been massacred and several thousand women had been raped in Nanjing, and called on the League to take action. 

In January 1938, an officer from Chiang Kai-shek’s army who had escaped from Nanjing after hiding there as a disguised soldier submitted a military report on the fall of the city to the Nationalist Army’s headquarters. If, by that time, the Republic of China had obtained verifiable evidence that the Japanese military was massacring Nanjing’s civilians, Gu Weijun would have included it in his speech. But the allegation of 20,000 killings was based on newspaper reports in the New York Times and elsewhere, which had in turn relied on hearsay from Professor Bates and Reverend Fitch. 
Bates was an adviser to the Republic of China, while Reverend Fitch is known as a suspicious figure who drove the perpetrator of the Shanghai Imperial Birthday Celebration bombing to the scene and then hid the mastermind of the bombing on the second floor of his home for a month.

Reporters such as A. T. Steele, who reported that “the Japanese military is massacring civilians in Nanjing,” were given housing by the Nationalist government. Professor Smythe of Jinling University wrote War Damage in the Nanking Area in June 1938, but the latest research has established that the Nationalist government’s International Propaganda Department funded its preparation.

Conclusion: The Nanjing Massacre was simply a battle. As the Nationalist Army’s commander-in-chief of the Nanjing Defense Force fled and the soldiers were left without command, some were killed by their own Barrier troops as they tried to escape Nanjing. Those who did escape killed civilians in order to take their clothing and change into it, becoming plainclothes soldiers. Their punishment as plainclothes soldiers has been labeled a massacre, but they were not entitled to prisoner-of-war status. The deaths in the Battle of Nanjing were simply deaths resulting from combat, killings by the blocking troops, and executions of plainclothes soldiers.

2. On 11 March 2026, Amit Shah told the Lok Sabha that members who don't follow the rules will have their mic turned off.

5. RG’s words get deleted. His Adani speech in 2023, his "Hindu" speech in 2024 and his Budget-session remarks in 2026 were all expunged. In a public debate, nothing can be deleted afterwards.

text:
Discipleship Is A Call to place Christ above Earthly Attachments & Personal Ambitions
————
Contact: enakhena@reborn.com

Memoria Sancti Caroli Borromeo, Episcopi 

Philippians 2:12-18-:
Key Verses-:"Work out your salvation with fear and trembling. For God is the one who, for his good purpose, works in you both to desire and to work. Do everything without grumbling or questioning..among whom you shine like lights in the world..."
Psalm 27:1, 4, 13–14-:
Key Verse "The Lord is my light and my salvation."
1 Peter 4:14-:
"If you are insulted for the name of Christ, blessed are you, for the Spirit of God rests upon you."
Luke 14:25-33-:
Key Verse- Jesus addresses the crowds: "Whoever does not carry his own cross and come after me cannot be my disciple... Which of you wishing to construct a tower does not first sit down and calculate the cost?... In the same way, everyone of you who does not renounce all his possessions cannot be my disciple."

Genuine discipleship requires commitment, sacrifice, humility, obedience and the willingness to place God above personal ambitions, possessions, relationships and worldly attachments. In Philippians 2, Apostle Paul encourages Christians to take their spiritual lives seriously. He reminds us that salvation is God’s work within us, enabling us both to desire what is good and to accomplish it.Paul also challenges believers to do everything without grumbling or unnecessary arguments so that they may become blameless children of God in a crooked and morally confused generation.
He describes Christians as people who must shine like lights in the world while holding firmly to the Word of Life. God offers us His grace, but we must respond through faith, obedience, repentance and good works.

We cannot claim to love God while deliberately continuing in dishonesty, exploitation, hatred, corruption or injustice.
Our faith must produce visible evidence of transformation. In Luke 14, Jesus addresses the great crowds following Him and explains the seriousness of Christian discipleship.
He teaches that anyone who wishes to become His disciple must place Him above every other attachment. He uses two illustrations: A. The Builder and the Tower (Luke 14:28–30)Before constructing a tower, a wise builder calculates the cost to determine whether he has sufficient resources to complete it.Jesus uses this example to teach that discipleship requires serious consideration, preparation and commitment.

Christianity is not a temporary emotional decision. It is a lifelong journey of faithfulness. Jesus describes a king who carefully considers whether his army is strong enough to confront another king.
The lesson is about recognising the seriousness of the undertaking before making a commitment. Following Christ requires spiritual discipline, wisdom and perseverance. (Luke 14:33)Jesus concludes by teaching that anyone who does not renounce all possessions cannot be His disciple.This don’t mean that every Christian must abandon family responsibilities, employment or material possessions.Rather, nothing must become more important than God.We must be willing to surrender anything that competes with our loyalty to Christ.

PRAYERS & MEDITATION 

Heavenly Father. Thank You for the gift of another day and for the grace to know and follow Your Son, Jesus Christ.Give me the wisdom to understand the cost of discipleship and the courage to surrender everything that separates me from Your love.Transform my heart, strengthen my faith and guide my decisions.
May my life become a testimony of Your goodness, truth, compassion and righteousness.
Lord Jesus, You ask for everything because You gave everything for me. Help me to renounce all self-centered desires, fears, and attachments that hold me back from true freedom. Work in me both the desire and the strength to serve You faithfully today. Amen.

text:
Why Code Geass Is One of the Greatest Written Anime of All Time. 🔥🔥🔥

Ichirō Ōkouchi is, in my opinion, one of the greatest screenwriters in the anime industry. Throughout his career, he has contributed to numerous high-quality productions, but today I want to focus on my personal favorite work of his: Code Geass: Lelouch of the Rebellion (2006–2007) and its second season, Code Geass: Lelouch of the Rebellion R2 (2008).

There are numerous reasons why I consider Code Geass such an exceptional anime, particularly regarding its writing. From its protagonist and supporting cast to its political intrigue, morally complicated characters, romance, and exploration of the consequences of war, the series offers an extraordinary amount to appreciate.

What makes it particularly impressive is how many characters feel like actual human beings. They possess individual motivations, shortcomings, prejudices, ambitions, emotional attachments, and conflicting perspectives. They aren't simply good or evil characters performing predetermined roles; they're individuals whose experiences influence their decisions.

One of the biggest reasons I love Code Geass is its protagonist, Lelouch vi Britannia.

Lelouch is an exceptionally intelligent strategist, but his intelligence doesn't make him infallible. I particularly appreciate that Ōkouchi doesn't portray him as a perfect mastermind who is always ten steps ahead of everyone else. Despite his extraordinary analytical abilities, Lelouch makes numerous mistakes, many of which have serious consequences.

One example occurs during his confrontation with Cornelia in Season 1. After experiencing considerable success against Britannian forces, Lelouch becomes increasingly confident in his abilities. Unfortunately, this confidence develops into arrogance.

Despite C.C. warning him that something isn't right, Lelouch underestimates Cornelia's experience and strategic capabilities. He assumes he can overcome her as he has overcome previous opponents, only to suffer a humiliating defeat.

Another example occurs during his chess match against Schneizel. Rather than calmly accepting that his brother might genuinely outmaneuver him, Lelouch interprets Schneizel's behavior as mockery and becomes emotionally frustrated, eventually forfeiting the game.

These moments demonstrate one of Lelouch's biggest weaknesses: his ego frequently interferes with his ability to make rational decisions. He can analyze military engagements and manipulate political situations, yet still allow his pride and emotional immaturity to dictate his actions.

This is precisely what makes him compelling. He's extraordinarily intelligent while simultaneously possessing very human weaknesses.

His motivations for rebelling against Britannia are equally interesting. Lelouch isn't simply an ordinary Japanese citizen who resents imperial occupation. He's actually a Britannian prince, the son of Emperor Charles zi Britannia, who once enjoyed the privileges associated with the imperial family.

However, everything changes following the assassination of his mother, Marianne vi Britannia.

After witnessing her death, Lelouch demands answers from his father and requests protection for himself and his disabled younger sister, Nunnally. Considering Charles is the emperor of the world's most powerful nation, Lelouch reasonably expects him to investigate the assassination and protect his children.

Instead, Charles dismisses their concerns, prioritizing imperial politics and the stability of his empire over his children's well-being.

Consequently, Lelouch and Nunnally are effectively abandoned and sent to Japan, which Britannia subsequently conquers and renames Area 11.

This establishes a deeply personal motivation for Lelouch's hatred of Britannia. His mother was murdered, his father refused to provide meaningful answers, and he and his sister were discarded when they became inconvenient.

Furthermore, his desire to create a better world for Nunnally gives his rebellion another dimension. He doesn't simply want revenge; he wants to establish a society where his sister can live peacefully without being discriminated against because of her disability.

The combination of personal tragedy, revenge, and genuine affection for someone he loves makes his motivations particularly compelling.

Another aspect of Ōkouchi's writing I appreciate is his willingness to explore the human consequences of leading a rebellion.

Lelouch frequently makes decisions that accomplish his military objectives while simultaneously causing innocent people to suffer.

One particularly memorable example occurs during the Narita campaign. Lelouch uses the surrounding terrain to trigger a massive landslide against Britannian forces, turning the environment into an effective weapon against a numerically superior opponent.

However, the destruction doesn't discriminate between combatants and civilians. Among its victims is Shirley's father.

This is important because it demonstrates that even Lelouch's military victories can come at an enormous human cost. His actions aren't taking place in a video game where defeating an opponent simply means accumulating points. They affect actual people, including individuals who have nothing to do with his rebellion.

I appreciate that the series explores the emotional consequences of these decisions. Lelouch isn't completely indifferent to the suffering he causes. As the story progresses, he increasingly confronts the reality that changing the world through violence involves accepting responsibility for the lives lost along the way.

His intelligence doesn't make him omniscient, either. Sometimes he lacks information, misunderstands someone's intentions, or fails to anticipate an unexpected reaction.

This makes his characterization considerably more believable. No matter how intelligent someone is, they cannot perfectly predict every individual's behavior or account for every variable in a battlefield situation.

Lelouch is exceptionally capable, but he's still human.

Lelouch's Intelligence and Strategic Thinking

Speaking of intelligence, another major reason I enjoy Lelouch is that the series actually demonstrates his strategic abilities through his decisions.

One of the best examples occurs during the Shinjuku incident in the first episode.

Initially, Lelouch is an ordinary student who secretly wants to overthrow Britannia. However, he accidentally becomes caught in a military operation involving Britannian forces and Japanese resistance fighters. During this incident, he acquires Geass, which allows him to issue absolute commands to people who make eye contact with him.

Although this supernatural ability is extraordinarily useful, Lelouch doesn't begin the series with an army, military reputation, or meaningful experience commanding soldiers.

Nevertheless, he manages to turn the situation to his advantage.

First, he recognizes the strategic importance of his surroundings, using Shinjuku's geography, unstable infrastructure, construction sites, and surrounding ruins to compensate for his lack of military resources.

Second, he understands that manipulating enemy behavior can be more effective than confronting opponents directly. He anticipates how Britannian soldiers will move and exploits their positioning.

Third, he recognizes the importance of psychological warfare. Despite having virtually no military experience, he presents himself as a capable commander who understands the situation and possesses a comprehensive plan.

Finally, he understands that Geass is most useful when employed to manipulate people's decisions rather than simply treating it as a straightforward weapon.

He combines his intelligence, psychological manipulation, and supernatural ability to overcome circumstances that would otherwise be virtually impossible for him.

I particularly appreciate that the series demonstrates his intelligence through actual strategic decisions instead of repeatedly having other characters announce how intelligent he is.

Another reason I love Lelouch is that he isn't a Mary Sue or an overpowered protagonist.

Despite possessing extraordinary intelligence and Geass, he has numerous shortcomings, and the narrative regularly punishes him for them.

His relationship with Suzaku provides an excellent example. Although they are childhood friends, they develop fundamentally different philosophies regarding how Britannia should be challenged.

Lelouch believes the empire must be defeated through revolution and military force, whereas Suzaku believes it should be reformed from within.

When Lelouch attempts to recruit Suzaku into the Black Knights, Suzaku refuses because he fundamentally disagrees with his methods.

This demonstrates that Lelouch cannot simply convince everyone to follow him. His intelligence, charisma, and Geass cannot automatically resolve ideological disagreements.

Another example involves Mao. During their confrontation, Lelouch makes the mistake of instructing people under Geass to shoot Mao if he attempts to reveal his secret without explicitly ordering them to kill him.

This seemingly minor oversight eventually comes back to haunt him when Mao becomes a threat to Nunnally.

I appreciate these moments because they demonstrate how Lelouch's personality can undermine his intelligence. He occasionally prioritizes theatrics, pride, and the satisfaction of outsmarting someone over simply accomplishing his objective.

Throughout the series, he also develops beyond his original motivations of revenge and protecting Nunnally. He increasingly recognizes the consequences of his actions and the responsibility associated with leading an organization capable of influencing millions of lives.

His journey eventually becomes about creating a better future and accepting responsibility for the suffering he has caused.

Kallen Kōzuki: A Strong Supporting Character With Genuine Depth

Lelouch isn't the only compelling character in Code Geass. Its supporting cast is another major strength, particularly Kallen Kōzuki, also known as Kallen Stadtfeld.

One of the most interesting aspects of Kallen's characterization is her struggle with identity.

Publicly, she's a Britannian student from a privileged family. Privately, however, she identifies strongly with her Japanese heritage and resents Britannia's occupation and mistreatment of the Japanese population, whom the empire derogatorily calls Elevens.

Despite enjoying a relatively comfortable lifestyle through her Britannian family connections, she willingly risks her life by joining the Japanese resistance.

Her decision is rooted in her personal experiences, Japanese identity, and the loss of her brother, making her involvement in the Black Knights feel like a meaningful commitment.

Her relationship with her mother is another particularly interesting aspect of her characterization.

Initially, Kallen despises her mother because she believes she willingly accepts humiliation from the Britannian mistress of their household. However, she eventually discovers that her mother's behavior is considerably more complicated than she initially understood.

Her mother struggles with drug addiction, and Kallen learns that her continued presence in the household and apparent submission were connected to her desire to remain close to and protect her daughter.

This revelation forces Kallen to reconsider her assumptions and recognize that she doesn't necessarily understand everything happening around her.

Kallen is also morally complicated. She's willing to kill for her cause, even when doing so involves ethically questionable decisions. Early in the series, when she suspects Lelouch has discovered her identity, she's prepared to eliminate him to protect herself and the resistance.

Furthermore, her experiences at school and relationships with Shirley and Nunnally gradually challenge her prejudices against Britannians. She becomes increasingly aware that nationality doesn't automatically determine someone's morality.

Her abilities as a Knightmare Frame pilot also give her an important role beyond her relationships with other characters. She's exceptionally talented, and her combat performance reflects her dedication and willingness to put herself in danger for the cause she believes in.

Finally, I also appreciate Kallen's physical attractiveness and character design. She's portrayed as a sexy, voluptuous woman with large breasts and an unmistakably feminine appearance. The series certainly isn't shy about incorporating fanservice into her presentation, and I personally enjoy that aspect of her character.

However, her sex appeal doesn't come at the expense of her characterization. She's allowed to possess a voluptuous figure, participate in fanservice, and simultaneously have meaningful motivations, ideological convictions, personal conflicts, and character development.

I appreciate that Ōkouchi allows Kallen to be both a sexually appealing anime character and a genuinely multidimensional supporting character. Those qualities aren't mutually exclusive.

Another major strength of Code Geass is Suzaku Kururugi, who serves as one of Lelouch's most important ideological opposites.

Rather than simply existing to obstruct the protagonist, Suzaku has his own philosophy and understanding of how society should change.

Where Lelouch believes Britannia must be defeated through revolution, Suzaku believes meaningful reform should happen within the existing political system.

Lelouch is willing to use deception, manipulation, and violence, whereas Suzaku places greater importance on following established rules and working through legitimate institutions.

Importantly, Suzaku makes some compelling arguments against Lelouch's methods. He recognizes that terrorism, deception, and military violence can cause innocent people to suffer.

At the same time, Lelouch's criticisms of Suzaku are understandable. Suzaku is attempting to reform an empire that systematically discriminates against Japanese people while simultaneously participating in its military structure.

Their conflict is compelling because neither character is arguing from an entirely nonsensical position. They have fundamentally different understandings of morality, political legitimacy, and how societies should change.

I particularly appreciate that Ōkouchi allows both characters to make arguments viewers can understand, even when they disagree with their conclusions.

Another aspect of Code Geass I appreciate is its willingness to explore racism, prejudice, and cruelty without suggesting that they're exclusive to one nationality.

Britannia operates according to a ruthless ideology involving social Darwinism, imperial dominance, and the belief that stronger civilizations have the right to dominate weaker ones.

Many Britannians genuinely believe their empire is creating a stronger and more orderly world. However, the consequences of this ideology are horrific.

One of the clearest examples occurs in Episode 1, following Britannia's invasion of Japan. Clovis la Britannia orders the massacre of Japanese civilians in the Shinjuku ghetto, treating them as disposable because they're classified as Elevens and considered inferior under Britannia's social hierarchy.

However, the series doesn't suggest Japanese people are automatically morally superior simply because they're victims of imperialism.

In Episode 12, Japanese terrorists take children hostage to generate political pressure and draw attention to their cause. Their opposition to Britannia doesn't automatically make their actions morally defensible.

Likewise, not every Britannian supports imperial oppression, just as not every Japanese resistance fighter possesses admirable intentions.

This makes the political environment considerably more believable. Individuals on both sides can demonstrate compassion, prejudice, ambition, cruelty, selflessness, and ideological extremism.

The conflict isn't reduced to an oversimplified narrative in which one nationality consists entirely of good people and the other consists entirely of bad people.

Another aspect of Code Geass I appreciate is how Ōkouchi incorporates romance, attraction, and sexuality into the narrative.

Personally, I've never particularly enjoyed anime protagonists who behave unrealistically whenever a woman expresses romantic interest in them. It can become difficult to take seriously when an otherwise intelligent and confident character suddenly becomes incapable of responding normally to a romantic advance.

That's one reason I appreciate Lelouch.

When Shirley kisses him during an emotional moment, he doesn't respond with exaggerated confusion. He understands the situation and accepts her affection, embracing her in the rain.

Similarly, when Kallen kisses him in Season 2, Lelouch doesn't immediately reject her or behave as though he has no understanding of romantic attraction.

I appreciate that he's portrayed as someone capable of acknowledging affection and responding naturally.

Other relationships are equally interesting. Suzaku and Euphemia's romance develops through their interactions and shared experiences, while Ohgi and Villetta's relationship is particularly compelling because they initially belong to opposing sides of the conflict.

Their feelings eventually become strong enough that they're willing to betray the interests of their respective factions to protect one another. Their eventual marriage and child demonstrate that personal relationships can extend beyond the military and political conflict surrounding them.

Romance in Code Geass isn't simply decorative. It influences character decisions, creates emotional conflicts, and occasionally has significant consequences for the broader narrative.

I also appreciate that Code Geass isn't afraid to incorporate fanservice, attractive female characters, and sexual themes.

Kallen is an obvious example, but C.C. is another character whose attractiveness and sexuality are incorporated into her presentation.

Personally, I don't see anything inherently wrong with attractive female characters having voluptuous figures, large breasts, revealing outfits, or occasional fanservice moments.

What matters is whether they possess personalities, motivations, and meaningful roles beyond their physical appearance.

Kallen and C.C. demonstrate that considerable sex appeal can coexist with genuine characterization and narrative importance.

Furthermore, the series demonstrates that personal attachments and sexuality can have serious consequences.

One particularly memorable example is Nina Einstein. Her obsession with Princess Euphemia, combined with the traumatic consequences of Euphemia's death, contributes to her increasingly unstable behavior and involvement in developing the F.L.E.I.J.A. weapon.

The consequences are catastrophic, with the weapon eventually causing enormous destruction and killing thousands of people.

Shirley is another example. Despite knowing that Lelouch is involved in extremely dangerous activities, her feelings for him eventually lead her to put herself at considerable risk to help him. Unfortunately, her involvement in his world contributes to her tragic fate in Season 2.

These examples demonstrate that love, attraction, jealousy, grief, and obsession can influence people's decisions, sometimes with devastating consequences.

Finally, one of the biggest reasons I consider Code Geass such a well-written anime is its political storytelling.

Rather than presenting the conflict as a straightforward struggle between good and evil, the series explores political legitimacy, propaganda, public perception, military strategy, nationalism, imperialism, and the preservation of political power.

Charles's treatment of Lelouch and Nunnally is an excellent example. Following Marianne's assassination, he prioritizes the stability and interests of the Britannian Empire over investigating the incident in a way that might destabilize the imperial family.

This demonstrates how political leaders can prioritize institutional stability and the preservation of power over even their own personal relationships.

Another example occurs during the Narita campaign.

Cornelia wants to eliminate the Black Knights, but she understands that simply using overwhelming military force isn't necessarily the most effective approach.

Thanks to Zero's theatrical presentation and carefully constructed public image, the Black Knights are beginning to establish themselves as protectors of the oppressed.

If Britannia indiscriminately massacres them, particularly in circumstances involving civilians, it risks transforming them into martyrs and generating even greater public sympathy for the resistance.

This demonstrates that even authoritarian governments must consider public perception and political legitimacy. Relying exclusively on violence can create instability and encourage additional resistance.

Lelouch understands this as well. Defeating Britannia militarily isn't enough; he must also influence how ordinary people perceive the conflict.

By presenting Zero as someone who protects the oppressed and challenges imperial oppression, he attempts to undermine Britannia's legitimacy while strengthening the reputation of the Black Knights.

Cornelia recognizes that the situation isn't simply a military engagement. It's also a political and propaganda battle.

I particularly appreciate this because it demonstrates that military commanders and political leaders must consider more than whether they can defeat an opponent on the battlefield. They must also consider public opinion, political legitimacy, and the broader consequences of their decisions.

This makes the political conflict considerably more sophisticated than a conventional anime narrative in which the protagonist simply defeats increasingly powerful enemies.

Overall, Code Geass is one of my favorite examples of exceptional anime writing and one of the strongest demonstrations of Ichirō Ōkouchi's storytelling abilities.

What makes the series so impressive is its combination of multidimensional characters, political intrigue, ideological conflicts, believable motivations, romantic relationships, and willingness to explore the consequences of violence.

Lelouch is an outstanding protagonist because he's intelligent without being infallible, ambitious without being entirely rational, and powerful without being immune to the consequences of his decisions. His ego, emotional vulnerabilities, personal motivations, and eventual development make him considerably more human than a protagonist who effortlessly outsmarts everyone.

The supporting cast is equally impressive. Kallen possesses a compelling identity conflict and meaningful development, while Suzaku provides an ideological counterweight to Lelouch, challenging his methods and forcing viewers to consider the morality of his decisions.

I also appreciate how the series approaches political and social issues. It doesn't portray entire nationalities as inherently good or evil, nor does it suggest that opposing an oppressive government automatically makes someone morally righteous.

The romance is another welcome aspect because characters are allowed to experience attraction, develop relationships, and respond to romantic advances without constantly behaving as though they cannot understand basic human interactions.

And, of course, I appreciate that the series incorporates attractive female characters, sexy designs, voluptuous figures, large breasts, and fanservice without necessarily sacrificing characterization or narrative importance.

Ultimately, what makes Code Geass stand out is how naturally its characters reflect human behavior. They make decisions based on personal experiences, ideological convictions, emotional attachments, ambition, revenge, self-preservation, and sometimes their own arrogance.

They aren't always rational, they don't always make the correct decisions, and they certainly don't always agree with one another.

That's precisely what makes the narrative so compelling.

Ōkouchi created a story in which military engagements have political consequences, romantic relationships influence personal decisions, ideological disagreements generate meaningful conflict, and even the protagonist's greatest victories can become sources of guilt and regret.

There are plenty of anime featuring intelligent protagonists, attractive female characters, political conflicts, and elaborate battle strategies. However, comparatively few manage to combine all these elements while giving their characters the depth, humanity, and internal contradictions that Code Geass possesses, all while bringing the story to a powerful emotional conclusion.

For me, Code Geass: Lelouch of the Rebellion is a masterpiece of anime storytelling. Outstanding work, Ichirō Ōkouchi! 👍

text:
As expected, Narendra modi doesn't appear to have the courage to accept Rahul Gandhi's challenge for an open public debate.
Instead of accepting the challenge, the entire BJP establishment, including its ministers and party leaders, has launched a coordinated attack on Rahul Gandhi. Suddenly, everyone is invoking Parliament and insisting that debates should take place there.But let me explain why Parliament, under the BJP government and Speaker Om Birla, can hardly be called a forum for genuine democratic debate.
Here are 10 reasons:
1. When the microphone is switched off :-
On 12 March 2026, Rahul Gandhi's microphone reportedly went silent in the middle of his speech, shortly after he referred to a minister allegedly describing himself as "a friend of Mr Epstein."
2. Even the Home Minister has openly talked about switching off microphones.
On 11 March 2026, Amit Shah told the Lok Sabha that members who failed to follow parliamentary rules would have their microphones switched off. Is that how a healthy democracy encourages debate ?
3. Certain names and subjects are apparently too uncomfortable to discuss.
On 12 March, the Speaker stopped Rahul Gandhi when he attempted to connect US claims concerning Russian oil with Hardeep Puri's name in the Epstein files.
4. Even a former Army Chief's memoir becomes off-limits.
In February 2026, Rahul Gandhi was prevented from quoting General MM Naravane's memoir while discussing China's activities and India's national security. If the government is confident about its decisions, why should such questions be avoided ?
5. The Opposition's words can simply be erased from the record.
Rahul Gandhi's remarks concerning Adani in 2023, his speech on Hinduism in 2024, and his Budget-session remarks in 2026 were expunged from parliamentary records. Imagine an open public debate where one side can simply delete the other side's arguments afterwards!
6. Suspend the Opposition and the government gets a much easier debate.
Eight MPs were suspended in February 2026, while a record 146 Opposition MPs were suspended in December 2023. What kind of democratic discussion is possible when elected representatives are removed from the House ?
7. Even the parliamentary cameras seem reluctant to show the Opposition leader.
On several occasions, when Rahul Gandhi is speaking, the cameras reportedly focus on BJP leaders or Speaker Om Birla instead of showing the person addressing the House. Even the visual coverage of parliamentary proceedings raises questions.
 
8. Even the neutrality of the referee is being questioned.
In March 2026, the Opposition moved a resolution seeking the removal of Speaker Om Birla. The resolution was defeated through a voice vote. When the Opposition itself questions the impartiality of the person chairing the proceedings, how can it be expected to have complete confidence in the fairness of the debate ?

So, Modi ji, why are you hesitating ?
Rahul Gandhi's offer is actually very generous. You can even choose the moderator or judge yourself ,he has reportedly indicated that even Mohan Bhagwat ji would be acceptable.
You can choose the platform too. Perhaps NDTV, Adani's media network, would make you more comfortable.
Choose the moderator. Choose the platform. Set the rules.
But please, come forward and face Rahul Gandhi in an open debate.
Because democracy is not just about delivering speeches when nobody can question you. It is also about having the courage to answer uncomfortable questions when the other side has an equal opportunity to respond.

text:
I let my sister believe her husband was cheating because I wanted her to cancel their anniversary trip and give me the tickets.

They had booked a week in Hawaii for their tenth anniversary. When my sister mentioned that she might not be able to go because of work, I immediately offered to take her place.

She laughed and said the tickets were nonrefundable anyway.

A few days later, I saw her husband’s phone light up while he was visiting our parents. A woman had sent him a message saying, “Last night was amazing. When can I see you again?”

I knew the woman. She was his coworker.

I took a picture of the notification and sent it to my sister.

What I didn’t tell her was that I’d seen the rest of the conversation. He had replied that she needed to stop sending personal messages because he was married.

text:
11 PM Top-of-the-Hour News

Election night in America 2026. I'm Matt Pieper.: “And I'm Stacy Lynn in Washington. President Trump made several trips to South Carolina to try to help Republican Darlene Graham hold on to a Senate seat. She is a natural and she's a great woman, so get out and vote. But it wasn't enough. Democrat Annie Andrews has defeated Graham, flipping a Republican-held Senate seat blue. South Carolina. You have shown the nation what is possible. Trump had rallied for Graham in South Carolina twice, including a stop just days before the election as the race grew unexpectedly competitive. But Andrews pulled off the upset, giving Democrats another Senate pickup. ”

In Georgia -
Keisha Lance Bottoms has been elected the country's first Black female governor.
Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff has been re-elected in Georgia -: “Let me be the first to offer public congratulations to the governor-elect of the state of Georgia, Keisha Lance Bottoms. ”

History also made in Florida.
Republican By-ron Donalds will be the next governor - defeating Democrat David Jolly.
He will be Florida's first Black governor -: “We are going to drive down costs for the people of this state. We are going to lower insurance premiums for the people of this state. We are going to make housing more affordable for the people of this state. We are going to protect the agricultural lands, our water, and our environment here for the future of this state. ”

Hakeem Jeffries has won re-election in New York's 8th Congressional district.
Jeffries is on track to make House speaker history - if he becomes the first Black House speaker.: “We are going to move expeditiously to solve the problems, particularly around the affordability crisis that the American people have decisively indicated throughout this campaign they want to see addressed with a fierce urgency. There's a lot of people. ”

In New Jersey -
Democrat Rebecca Bennett, a former Navy helicopter pilot, has defeated two-term Rep. Tom Kean Jr., who missed four months of votes in Washington this year as he underwent treatment for depression, a diagnosis he did not disclose until his return.
Kean represents a battleground district that includes Trump’s Bedminster golf club.
His great-grandfather was a senator, his grandfather was a congressman, and his father is the former two-term Gov. Tom Kean Sr.

Democrat Roy Cooper won North Carolina’s Senate race, the first Democratic pickup of the night, and Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff was reelected in Georgia, another top battleground.
Democrats have flipped four House seats.
If they hold on to all the districts they currently represent, that’s enough to win the majority.
Republicans could pick up a handful of Democratic seats in states that redrew their district boundaries.
All eyes are on Senate contests in Alaska, Iowa, Kansas, Maine, Michigan, Ohio and Texas.
Polls close right now in California and Washington.
At 12am - they close in Hawaii.
At 1am - Alaska.

Even working at the International Space Station - has not kept astronaut Anil Menon from casting his ballot - as a resident of Harris County, Texas.
He offered a quick snapshot on social media - of the process of voting from space.: “This is my room that doubles as a voting booth for me. Inside of it is my computer where I was able to fill out an electronic form and send it to Harris County, so I could vote. ”
Crewmates Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney did the same.

Uruguay has unveiled the popemobile that Pope Leo will use during his visit this week to South America.
Local manufacturer NORDEX says the vehicle - which started as a donated Fiat - was built to Vatican specifications.
That includes protection from adverse weather, accessibility and safety during travel.
It earned Cardinal Daniel Sturla's blessing. He noted the quality of the work - suggesting it was carried out impeccably.  He says it will allow the pope to stand if he so chooses.
Pope Leo is set to visit 10 cities during his South American tour beginning Friday - which also includes stops in Argentina and Peru.

text:
A historic defeat for the traditional online sports betting industry appears to be looming in the US state of Nebraska, the only state voting on the topic this election.

Despite $23 million to $0 in support of legalizing it (according to Nebraska Plains Ledger data), the measure appears to be in big trouble. Only 41% of votes have been counted as of this post, but the tally for legalizing online sports betting is down ~7 points (NYT/AP).

Nebraska would be just the second state after California in 2022 to reject legalizing online sports betting at the ballot box.

Legal online sports gambling isn't as controversial as AI data centers, but it's quite unpopular.

An Overton Insights poll from May found American voters opposed legalization 47% to 31%.

Prediction markets, which offer sports betting outside state regulation, are even more controversial, according to other polling.

Eight years after the Supreme Court overturned the federal prohibition, U.S. online sports betting has run amok, according to numerous public health experts and policymakers I've interviewed. The public appears to be turning on it. Even if Nebraskans narrowly approve it, the industry is losing favor with the American public.

As a result, public health reform related to online gambling is gaining momentum.

text:
Happy Birthday Cameron Mitchell

Mitchell was an extraordinarily versatile, but difficult actor whose career lasted 55 years. His name may not be instantly recognisable, but anyone who has seen “How to Marry a Millionaire” will remember him as Lauren Bacall’s spunky young suitor. Not conventionally handsome, he was, nonetheless, engaging. Mitchell was born in 1918, in Dallastown, Pennsylvania. In 1939, after two years of trying to break into acting, he wrote dozens of letters to actors, agents, and producers. On receiving no response, he said, "I was bitter, mad at everyone. I sat down and wrote a letter to Alfred Lunt. It was the world's worst letter. I hate to think about it. I said I was a better actor than he was, but I was never going to get a chance to prove it". The somewhat tactless missive ended, "If you think you can act, you should see me". To Mitchell’s amazement, Lunt answered and offered him an audition. He apologised profusely for his rudeness, only for Lunt’s wife, actress Lynn Fontanne, to reassure him:”Don't worry about what you've done. Acting is your life's work, and you're not only going to be a good actor, but you're going to be a great actor". His agent, Ronald Leif, described Mitchell's ability thus: “A true actor isn't tagged. He isn't a heavy, a comic or a juvenile – he can assume any personality the role demands and play it convincingly. Such a man is Cameron Mitchell".  In 1945, he was signed to MGM. Mitchell had a minor part in “They Were Expendable” (1945), with John Wayne and Robert Montgomery. He appeared with Lana Turner and Spencer Tracy in “Cass Timberlane”, and with Wallace Beery in “The “Mighty McGurk” (both 1947). Mitchell moved to Columbia and had his first starring role as a prizefighter in the film noir “Leather Gloves” (1948). He also played Happy Loman in the 1951 film adaptation of “Death of a Salesman.” The actor then went to 20th Century-Fox, where he had a prolific career in films such as “Les Misérables” (1952), and the hugely successful “How to Marry a Millionaire” (1953), with Marilyn Monroe, Lauren Bacall and Betty Grable. He appeared alongside Gary Cooper, Susan Hayward, and Richard Widmark in “Garden of Evil” (1954), and had a major role in “Hell and High Water” (1954). Mitchell then co-starred with Marlon Brando in “Désirée”(1954); with Clark Gable and Jane Russell in the Western “The Tall Men” (1955); and appeared in the film musical “Carousel” (1956). He was loaned back to MGM to co-star with Doris Day and James Cagney in the outstanding drama “Love Me or Leave Me” (1955), in which he gave a moving performance as Day’s lover. Mitchell achieved huge success on television as the former Confederate soldier, drunken cowhand Buck Cannon in “The High Chaparral,”which aired from 1967 to 1971. He was famously hard to please, and quarrelled with all his colleagues. Throughout the 1960s, he starred in numerous exploitation films, including Italian sword and sandal epics, horror films, and thrillers, several of which were directed by Mario Bava, including “Erik the Conqueror” (1961), “Blood and Black Lace” (1964), and “Knives of the Avenger” (1966). In the late ‘70s and ‘80s, determined not to retire, Mitchell took roles in low-budget, direct-to-video films, which caused him to become a running gag on the internet film review show “Best of the Worst.” Cameron Mitchell died in 1994, in Pacific Palisades, California, aged 75.

text:
HOLD YOUR HEAD HIGH. THE WORK IS JUST BEGINNING.

Tonight, South Carolina has elected Annie Andrews to the United States Senate.

There will undoubtedly be plenty of finger-pointing in the days ahead. Some will look for someone to blame. Some will insist that voters who refused to support the Republican nominee are responsible for this outcome.

But to every South Carolinian who chose to write in Ralph Norman, we want to make one thing absolutely clear:

You have nothing to apologize for. Nothing to be ashamed of. And absolutely no reason to regret exercising your right to vote your conscience.

Your vote belonged to you. Not to a political party. Not to a candidate. Not to anyone who demanded your loyalty.

You made your own decision, and you had every right to make it.

On September 3rd, Write-In Ralph was nothing more than an idea. We had no political establishment behind us, no enormous campaign budget, and no institutional machinery.

What we had was a belief that voters deserved a choice.

And thousands of conversations later, that idea has grown into something none of us could have imagined when we started.

We didn't create the frustration that existed within the Republican electorate. We didn't create the divisions or the questions surrounding the nomination process.

We simply gave people a place to express themselves and an opportunity to make their voices heard.

And whatever tonight's results reveal, the responsibility for earning voters' support belongs to the candidates and the institutions that nominate them. It does not belong to voters who exercise their freedom of choice.

But tonight must also mark a turning point.

We cannot keep repeating the same mistakes and expecting different results. We cannot continue treating voter dissatisfaction as disloyalty rather than an opportunity to listen, learn, and improve.

And we cannot wait until the next election to begin addressing the problems that brought us here.

That work starts now.

In the months and years ahead, we intend to work toward a more accountable, transparent, and representative Republican nomination process. We want future nominees to earn the confidence of the people they hope to represent, rather than simply expect their votes.

That means getting involved, organizing, asking difficult questions, and working to ensure that grassroots voices have a meaningful place in the party's future.

To everyone who stood with Write-In Ralph: stand tall tonight.

You helped create an option where none had been offered. You stood for a principle even when others pressured you to abandon it. And you demonstrated that political participation doesn't begin and end with the choices printed on a ballot.

No election result can take that away from you.

This movement began with a simple belief: the people should have the final say.

That belief hasn't changed. And neither has our determination to defend it.

Your Vote. Your Voice. Your Choice.

🚨 AMY ACTON FLIPS OHIO GOVERNOR’S MANSION, DEFEATING VIVEK RAMASWAMY

COLUMBUS, UNITED STATES - A state that had been treated as reliably Republican at the statewide level has just shown that candidate quality and campaign execution still matter. Ohio voters did not simply choose between two parties; they rejected a campaign that increasingly revolved around personal attacks while rewarding a candidate who remained focused on issues affecting daily life.

For Republicans, the result creates an uncomfortable question about whether national political fame automatically translates into statewide success. Ramaswamy entered with advantages that many candidates never get, yet those advantages proved insufficient in a race decided by local perceptions and voter trust.

Democrats will study this result closely because it offers a possible roadmap in states that appear difficult on paper. If Acton’s coalition holds beyond a single election, Ohio could become far more competitive in statewide contests than many strategists assumed only a few years ago. The next test will be whether this victory remains an exception or becomes the start of a broader shift in Ohio politics.

text:
LETTERS FROM STOCKHOLM

AMERICA IS NOT FOR SALE: THE DEMOCRATIC COMEBACK AND A LESSON FOR NIGERIA

When the ballot box challenges the billionaire’s cheque book, democracy reminds the powerful who really owns a nation.

By Kio Amachree | President, Worldview International
Stockholm, Sweden | 4 November 2026

There are moments in the history of a democracy when ordinary citizens remind the political establishment that power does not belong to presidents, billionaires, political parties or wealthy financiers. It belongs to the people.

The American midterm elections of November 3 have produced one such moment.

The Democratic Party has staged a remarkable comeback, winning extraordinary Senate victories in Texas and South Carolina, making significant gains in the House of Representatives and challenging the political dominance of Donald Trump and the Republican Party.

The results are particularly remarkable because of the enormous sums of money invested in preserving Republican control of Washington.

Nowhere was this more apparent than in Texas.

For decades, Texas has been considered a Republican stronghold. Yet Democrat James Talarico defeated Republican Ken Paxton in a Senate contest that attracted extraordinary financial intervention from Elon Musk, the world’s wealthiest man.

Musk reportedly committed nearly $190 million to the Texas Senate contest, while his nationwide political spending exceeded $400 million during the midterm campaign.

Think about that for a moment.

Hundreds of millions of dollars poured into American politics by one extraordinarily wealthy individual, yet the voters of Texas demonstrated that financial power does not guarantee electoral victory.

There is something profoundly encouraging about that result.

It challenges the increasingly dangerous assumption that modern democracy is simply an auction in which the highest bidder purchases the government.

A billionaire may purchase advertising, political influence and an army of campaign consultants. He cannot automatically purchase the conscience of a nation.

The wider election results have raised serious questions about the direction of the Trump presidency.

American voters have expressed deep concerns about the cost of living, government accountability, political division and the concentration of power. Exit polling indicated substantial dissatisfaction with the country’s direction and strong public support for greater congressional checks on presidential authority.

The administration and its supporters will undoubtedly offer their own explanations for these defeats. That is their democratic right.

But the results have demonstrated that political loyalty is not unconditional and that even the most powerful political movements remain answerable to the electorate.

There is a lesson here that extends far beyond America’s borders.

FROM WASHINGTON TO ABUJA

I have watched political developments in Nigeria with increasing concern, particularly the growing influence of money, political patronage and the extraordinary privileges enjoyed by those close to power.

Under President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, Nigerians continue to debate serious questions about corruption, public spending, political accountability, electoral credibility and the widening distance between the governing elite and ordinary citizens.

These concerns deserve answers, not intimidation or political propaganda.

The parallels with America are worth examining, although the two countries have very different political institutions and electoral histories.

In both societies, citizens are entitled to ask whether their governments serve the public interest or the interests of powerful political and financial networks.

They are entitled to demand that public office be treated as a responsibility rather than an opportunity for private enrichment.

And they are entitled to reject attempts to divide communities along ethnic, racial or religious lines for political advantage.

Nigeria’s political class should study what happened in Texas.

The electorate cannot be treated indefinitely as a commodity to be bought, manipulated or taken for granted.

THE POWER OF THE ORDINARY CITIZEN

Democracy is not merely the privilege of voting every four years. It is the continuing right of citizens to question their leaders, investigate their conduct and remove them peacefully through credible elections.

The American midterms have illustrated how public dissatisfaction can translate into electoral consequences, even against candidates supported by extraordinary wealth.

That does not mean money has ceased to influence American politics. Far from it. The scale of campaign spending remains a legitimate cause for concern.

Nor does an electoral defeat automatically establish wrongdoing by those who financed the losing campaign.

But it does establish something important: financial resources alone cannot determine every election.

For Nigeria, the challenge is to build institutions capable of protecting that principle.

Independent electoral administration, transparent campaign financing, impartial courts, freedom of expression and security agencies that serve the constitution rather than political officeholders are essential to any credible democracy.

No political party should assume that its access to government resources gives it permanent ownership of the country.

No president should confuse the privileges of office with a personal mandate to govern without accountability.

And no wealthy political sponsor should imagine that an entire population can be reduced to a collection of purchasable votes.

A MESSAGE OF HOPE FOR NIGERIA

I have always believed that Nigeria possesses the human talent, resources and democratic potential to become one of the world’s most successful nations.

What Nigerians need is not another wealthy political godfather promising salvation, but institutions that protect their rights and leaders who understand the obligations of public service.

The American elections provide a timely reminder that political fortunes can change dramatically when citizens organise, participate and insist upon accountability.

Nigeria’s future must be determined by Nigerians themselves, through peaceful democratic participation and elections whose results genuinely reflect the public will.

Electoral malpractice, intimidation and vote-buying must be confronted through the law, independent institutions and vigilant public scrutiny.

The message from America is not that democracy has suddenly been perfected. It is that democracy retains the capacity to correct its course.

And that is a message worth celebrating.

The wealthy may finance political campaigns. Presidents may command enormous institutions. Political parties may build formidable electoral machines.

But none of them owns the nation.

America is not for sale. Nigeria should not be for sale either.

The ballot belongs to the citizen, the government belongs to the people, and the future belongs to those prepared to defend their democratic rights.

That is the enduring lesson of November 3.

Kio Amachree
President, Worldview International
Stockholm, Sweden

text:
U.S. Votes. Asia’s Chips Take the Hit. | November 4, 2026
📍Data From https://t.co/rtKhA53pFF Daily Report

The ballots are American.

The selling pressure has crossed the Pacific. 👀

Asian technology shares turned lower as early Democratic gains increased expectations of tougher scrutiny of AI and Big Tech.

Korean chip heavyweights came under pressure, while Japanese equities also fell sharply. These are intraday moves—not closing results—and congressional control remained unresolved in the reporting reviewed.

My trading read: investors are repricing policy risk before they can measure its impact on orders.

🏛️ 1. Why Washington matters to Asian hardware

The transmission channel is straightforward:

More scrutiny of US data centers → potentially higher costs or longer project timelines → uncertainty around equipment deployment → pressure on supplier earnings expectations.

Korean memory makers, Taiwanese semiconductor companies and Japanese equipment suppliers all have exposure to that spending cycle.

But this is a potential transmission path. Today’s selling does not establish that customers have cancelled orders.

🧠 2. A regulatory headline can hit valuations before revenue

Investors do not need to see an earnings downgrade before demanding a lower valuation.

If the expected timing or reliability of future cash flows becomes less certain, the price they will pay for those profits can fall immediately.

That helps explain why healthy current demand may offer limited protection during a policy-driven selloff.

📉 3. Lower Treasury yields aren’t an automatic rescue

Early reporting showed US equity futures falling alongside Treasury yields and the dollar.

Lower yields can support growth-stock valuations. But that benefit may be overwhelmed if investors simultaneously reduce their expectations for investment and earnings.

“Rates down” is only half the trade.

⚖️ 4. More oversight does not mean an immediate construction freeze

Congressional investigations, new legislation, federal executive actions and local permitting are different mechanisms.

The crucial question is what changes in actual project economics: approvals, power access, construction schedules and customer payments.

A political narrative becomes a fundamental problem when those operating measures deteriorate.

📋 What I would watch next

• Final congressional outcomes and specific policy proposals.
• US semiconductor performance when regular trading begins.
• Foreign flows and market breadth in Korea and Taiwan.
• Customer capital-expenditure plans and supplier guidance.
• Whether rebounds attract sustained buying.

If orders hold while policy fears stabilize, the selloff could create opportunities. If project delays and earnings cuts follow, a cheaper stock may simply reflect weaker cash flows.
Would you buy the policy scare—or wait for the spending outlook to prove resilient?
