text:
The Twenty-Third Sunday After Pentecost: From The Liturgical Year of Dom Prosper Gueranger.
.
.
Green Semi-double.
.
For the years when the number of the Sundays after Pentecost is only twenty-three, the Mass for today is taken from the twenty-fourth and last Sunday: and the Mass appointed for the twenty-third, is said on the previous Saturday, or on the nearest day of the preceding week, which is not impeded by a double or semi-double feast.
.
But, under all circumstances, the Antiphonary ends today. The Introits, Graduals, Communions, and Postcommunions, which are given below, are to be repeated on each of the Sundays till Advent, which may be more or less in number, according to the Years. Our readers will remember how, in the time of St. Gregory, Advent was longer than we now have it; and that, in those days, its weeks commenced in that part of the Cycle, which is now occupied by the last Sundays after Pentecost. This is one of the reasons which explain there being a lack of liturgical riches in the composition of the dominical Masses which follow the twenty-third.
.
Even on this one, formerly, the Church, without losing sight of the Last Day, used to lend a thought to the new season which was fast approaching, the season, that is, of preparation for the great feast of Christmas. There used to be read, as Epistle, the following passage from Jeremias, which was afterwards, in several Churches, inserted in the Mass of the first Sunday of Advent: Behold! the days come, saith the Lord, and I will raise up to David a just branch: and a King shall reign, and shall be wise: and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth. In those days, shall Juda be saved, and Israel shall dwell confidently: and this is the name that they shall call Him: The Lord our Just One. Therefore, behold the days come, saith the Lord, and they shall say no more: The Lord liveth, Who brought up the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt! But: The Lord liveth, Who hath brought out, and brought hither, the seed of the house of Israel, from the land of the north, and out of all the lands, to which I had cast them forth! And they shall dwell in their own land.
.
As is evident, this passage is equally applicable to the conversion of the Jews, and the restoration of Israel, which are to take place at the end of the world. This was the view taken by the chief liturgists of the Middle Ages, in order to explain thoroughly the Mass of the twenty-third Sunday after Pentecost. First mentioning to our readers, that, originally, the Gospel of this Sunday was that of the multiplication of the five loaves, let us listen to the profound and learned Abbot Rupert, who, better than anyone, will teach us the mysteries of this day, which brings to a close the grand and varied Gregorian Melodies, that we have been having during the whole year.
.
“Holy Church,” says he, “is so intent on paying her debt of supplication, and prayer, and thanksgiving, for all men, as the Apostle demands, that we find her giving thanks also for the salvation of the children of Israel, who, she knows, are one day to be united with her. And, as their remnants are to be saved at the end of the world, so, on this last Sunday of the Year, she delights at having them, just as though they were already her members! In the Introit, calling to mind the prophecies concerning them, she thus sings every Year: My thoughts are thoughts of peace, and not of affliction. Verily, His thoughts are those of peace, for He promises to admit to the banquet of his grace, the Jews, who are His brethren, according to the flesh; thus realizing what had been prefigured in the history of the patriarch Joseph. The brethren of Joseph, having sold him, came to him, when they were tormented by hunger; for then he ruled over the whole land of Egypt; he recognized them, he received them, and made, together with them, a great feast; so, too, our Lord Who is now reigning over the whole earth, and is giving the bread of life, in abundance, to the Egyptians (that is, to the Gentiles), will see coming to Him the remnants of the children of Israel. He, whom they had denied and put to death, will admit them to His favor, will give them a place at His table, and the true Joseph will feast delightedly with his brethren.
.
“The benefit of this divine Table is signified, in the Office of this Sunday, by the Gospel, which tells us of our Lord’s feeding the multitude with five loaves. For, it will be then, that Jesus will open to the Jews the five books of Moses, which are now being carried whole, and not yet broken,—yea, carried by a child, that is to say, this people itself, who, up to that time, will have been cramped up in the narrowness of a childish spirit.
.
“Then will be fulfilled the prophecy of Jeremias, which is so aptly placed before this Gospel: They shall say no more: The Lord liveth, Who brought up the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt! But, the Lord liveth, Who hath brought out of the seed of Israel from the land of the north, and from all the lands into which they had been cast.
.
“Thus delivered from the spiritual bondage which still holds them, they will sing with all their heart, the words of thanksgiving as we have them in the Gradual: Thou hast saved us, O Lord, from them that afflict us!
.
“The words we use in the Offertory: From the depths I have cried to Thee, O Lord, clearly allude to the same events; for, on that day, His brethren will say to the great and true Joseph: We beseech Thee to forget the wickedness of Thy brethren! The Communion: Amen, I say to you, all things whatsoever ye ask, when ye pray, &c., is the answer made by that same Joseph, as it was by the first: Fear not! Ye thought evil against Me: but God turned it into good, that He might exalt Me, as at present ye see, and might save many people. Fear not, therefore, I will feed you, and your children.”
.
Mass.—The Introit, which we have just had explained to us by Rupert, it taken from the Prophet Jeremias, as was the ancient Epistle.
.
Introit
.
Dicit Dominus: Ego cogito cogitationes pacis, et non afflictionis: invocabitis me, et ego exaudiam vos: et reducam captivitatem vestram de cunctis locis.
.
The Lord saith: I think thoughts of peace, and not of affliction; ye shall call upon Me, and I will hear you: and bring back your captive people from all places.
.
Ps. Benedixisti, Domine, terram tuam: avertisti captivitatem Jacob. Gloria Patri. Dicit Dominus.
.
Ps. Thou, O Lord, hast blessed Thy land: Thou hast brought back the captive children of Jacob. Glory, &c. The Lord.
.
Prayer for pardon is continually on the lips of the Christian people, because the weakness of human nature is, here below, ever making itself felt, even by the just man. God knows our frailty, and He is always ready to pardon us; but it is on the condition, that we humbly acknowledge our faults, and have confidence in His mercy. These are the sentiments which suggest to the Church the words of the Collect.
.
Collect
.
Absolve, quæsumus Domine, tuorum delicta populorum: ut a peccatorum nexibus, quæ pro nostra fragilitate contraximus, tua benignitate liberemur. Per Dominum.
.
Absolve, O Lord, we beseech Thee, the sins of Thy people; that, by Thy clemency, we may be delivered from the bonds of sins contracted by our own frailty. Through, &c.
.
The other Collects, as in the Fourth Sunday After Pentecost.
.
Epistle
.
Lectio Epistolæ beati Pauli Apostoli ad Philippenses. 
.
Lesson of the Epistle of St. Paul the Apostle, to the Philippians.
.
Cap. iii et iv. Ch. iii and iv.
.
Fratres, Imitatores mei estote, fratres, et observate eos qui ita ambulant, sicut habetis formam nostram. Multi enim ambulant, quos saepe dicebam vobis (nunc autem et flens dico) inimicos crucis Christi: quorum finis interitus: quorum Deus venter est: et gloria in confusione ipsorum, qui terrena sapiunt. Nostra autem conversatio in cælis est: unde etiam Salvatorem exspectamus Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, qui reformabit corpus humilitatis nostræ, configuratum corpori claritatis suæ, secundum operationem, qua etiam possit subjicere sibi omnia. Itaque fratres mei carissimi, et desideratissimi, gaudium meum, et corona mea: sic state in Domino, carissimi. Evodiam rogo, et Syntychen deprecor, idipsum sapere in Domino. Etiam rogo et te, germane compar, adjuva illas, quæ mecum laboraverunt in Evangelio cum Clemente, et ceteris adjutoribus meis, quorum nomina sunt in libro vitæ.
.
Brethren: Be ye followers of me, brethren, and observe them who walk so as you have our model. For many walk, of whom I have told you often (and now tell you weeping), that they are enemies of the cross of Christ; Whose end is destruction; whose God is their belly; and whose glory is in their shame; who mind earthly things. But our conversation is in heaven; from whence also we look for the Saviour, our Lord Jesus Christ, Who will reform the body of our lowness, made like to the body of His glory, according to the operation whereby also He is able to subdue all things unto Himself. Therefore, my dearly beloved brethren, and most desired, my joy and my crown; so stand fast in the Lord, my dearly beloved. I beg of Evodia, and I beseech Syntyche, to be of one mind in the Lord. And I entreat thee also, my sincere companion, help those women who have laboured with me in the gospel, with Clement and the rest of my fellow labourers, whose names are in the book of life.
.
The Clement, whose name is here mentioned by the Apostle, is that of St. Peter’s second successor. Very frequently, the twenty-third Sunday after Pentecost comes close upon the feast of this great Pope and Martyr of the first century. Disciple of Paul, and, later on, in close intimacy with Peter, and named by the Vicar of Christ as the fittest to succeed him in the apostolic chair,—Clement, as we shall see on the 23rd of November, was one of those Saints, who, in those early times, were the most venerated by the Faithful. The mention made of him, in the Office of the Time, just before his appearance on the Cycle of holy Church, excited the Christian people to joy, and roused its fervor; it reminded them, that one of their best and dearest protectors would soon be visiting them.
At the time when St. Paul was writing to the Philippians, Clement, who was long to survive the Apostles, was prominently one of those men spoken of in our Epistle,—that is, one of the followers of those illustrious models, who were called to perpetuate in the flock confided to their care, the pattern, of holy living; and that, not so much by their zealous teaching, as by the force of example. The Church, the One true Bride of the divine Word, was known by the incommunicable privilege of possessing within her the Truth,—not only its dead letter, but its ever living self, and this, by her holiness. The Holy Ghost has not kept the books of sacred Scripture from passing into the hands of the sects separated from the center of unity; but, he has reserved to the Church the treasure of tradition, which transmits, surely and fully, from one generation to another, the Word who is light and life; yes, this tradition is kept up by the truth and holiness of the Man-God; they are ever existing in his members, they are ever tangible and visible in the Church. Holiness, which is inherent in the Church, is tradition in its purest and strongest form, because it is the truth, not only preached, but reduced to action and work, as it was in Christ Jesus, and as it is in God. It is the deposit, which the disciples of the Apostles had the mission to hand faithfully down to their successors, just as the Apostles themselves had received it from the Word, who had come upon the earth.
.
Hence, St. Paul did not content himself with entrusting dogmatic teaching to his disciple Timothy; he said to him: Be thou an example to the Faithful, in word, and in living. He said much the same to Titus: Show thyself an example of good works, in doctrine and in integrity of life. He repeated to all: Be ye followers of me, as I also am of Christ. He sent Timothy to the Corinthians, that he might remind them, or, where it was necessary, might teach them, not only the dogmas of his Gospel, but, likewise, his ways in Christ Jesus, that is, his manner of life; for, this manner of life of the Apostle was, in a certain measure, his teaching everywhere in all the Churches; and he lauded the Faithful of Corinth for their being mindful to imitate him in all things, which was a keeping to the tradition of Christ. As for the Thessalonians, they had so thoroughly entered into this teaching, taken from their Apostle’s life, that, as St. Paul says of them, they had become a pattern to all believers; this silent teaching of Christian revelation, which they showed forth in their conduct, made it superfluous for the messengers of the Gospel to say much.
.
The Church is a magnificent Temple, which is built up, to the glory of God, by the living stones which let themselves be set into its walls. The constructing of those sacred walls, and on the plan laid down by Christ, is a work in which all are permitted to share. What one does by word, another does by good example; but, both of them build, both of them edify the holy City; and, as it was in the Apostolic Age, so always,—example is more powerful than word, unless that word be backed by the authority of holiness in him who speaks it, unless, that is, he lead a life according to the perfection taught by the Gospel.
.
But, as the giving edification to those around him, is an obligation incumbent on the Christian,—an obligation imposed both by charity he owes to his neighbor, and by the zeal he should have for the house of God,—so, likewise, under pain of presumption, he should seek his own edification in the conduct of others. The reading of good books, the study of the Lives of the Saints, the observing, as our Epistle says, the respectfully observing those holy people with whom he lives,—all this will be incalculable aid to him, in the work of his own personal sanctification and in the fulfilment of God’s purposes in his regard. This devout intercourse with the elect of earth and heaven, will keep us away from men who are enemies of the Cross of Christ and mind earthly things, and put their happiness in carnal pleasures. It will make our conversation be in heaven. Preparing for the day which cannot now be far off,—the day of the Coming of our Lord, we shall stand fast in Him, in spite of the falling off of so many amongst us, who, by the current of the world’s fashion, are hurried into perdition. The troubles and sufferings of the last times will but intensify our hope in God, for they will make us long all the more ardently for the happy day, when our Redeemer will appear and complete the work of the salvation of His servants, by imparting, to their very flesh, the brightness of His own divine Body. Let us, as our Apostle says, be of one mind in the Lord; and, then, as he bids his dear Philippians do, let us rejoice in the Lord always, yes, let us rejoice, for, the Lord is nigh.
.
Gradual
.
Liberasti nos, Domine, ex affligentibus nos: et eos qui nos oderunt, confudisti.
.
Thou hast saved us, O Lord, from them that afflict us: and hast put them to shame that hate us.
.
℣. In Deo laudabimur tota die, et in nomine tuo confitebimur in sæcula.
.
℣. In God shall we glory all the day long; and, in Thy name, we will give praise for ever.
.
Alleluia, alleluia.
.
Alleluia, alleluia.
.
℣. De profundis clamavi ad te, Domine: Domine exaudi orationem meam. Alleluia.
.
℣. Out of the depths I have cried unto Thee, O Lord: Lord, hear my prayer. Alleluia.
.
Gospel
.
Sequentia sancti Evangelii secundum Matthæum.
.
Sequel of the holy Gospel according to St. Matthew.
.
Cap.ix. Ch. ix.
.
In illo tempore: Loquente Jesu ad turbas, ecce princeps unus accessit, et adorabat eum, dicens: Domine, filia mea modo defuncta est: sed veni, impone manum tuam super eam, et vivet. Et surgens Jesus, sequebatur eum, et discipuli ejus. Et ecce mulier, quae sanguinis fluxum patiebatur duodecim annis, accessit retro, et tetigit fimbriam vestimenti ejus. Dicebat enim intra se: Si tetigero tantum vestimentum ejus, salva ero. At Jesus conversus, et videns eam, dixit: Confide, filia, fides tua te salvam fecit. Et salva facta est mulier ex illa hora. Et cum venisset Jesus in domum principis, et vidisset tibicines et turbam tumultuantem, dicebat: Recedite: non est enim mortua puella, sed dormit. Et deridebant eum. Et cum ejecta esset turba, intravit: et tenuit manum ejus, et surrexit puella. Et exiit fama haec in universam terram illam.
.
At that time: As Jesus was speaking to the multitude: Behold a certain ruler came up, and adored Him, saying: Lord, my daughter is even now dead; but come, lay thy hand upon her, and she shall live. And Jesus rising up followed him, with his disciples. And behold a woman who was troubled with an issue of blood twelve years, came behind him, and touched the Hem of his garment. For she said within herself: If I shall touch only His garment, I shall be healed. But Jesus turning and seeing her, said: Be of good heart, daughter, thy faith hath made thee whole. And the woman was made whole from that hour. And when Jesus was come into the house of the ruler, and saw the minstrels and the multitude making a rout, He said: Give place, for the girl is not dead, but sleepeth. And they laughed Him to scorn. And when the multitude was put forth, He went in, and took her by the hand. And the maid arose. And the fame hereof went abroad into all that country.
.
Although the choice of this Gospel for the twenty-third Sunday has not great antiquity on its side, yet is it in most perfect keeping with the post-pentecostal Liturgy, and confirms what we have stated, relative to the character of this portion of the Church’s Year. St. Jerome tells us, in the homily selected for the day, that the Hemorrhoissa, healed by our Lord, is a type of the Gentile world; while the Jewish people is represented by the daughter of the Ruler of the Synagogue. This latter is not to be restored to life, until the former has been cured; and this is precisely the mystery we are so continually commemorating during these closing weeks of the Liturgical Year,—the fullness of the Gentiles recognizing the welcoming the divine Physician, and the blindness of Israel, at last giving way to the Light.
.
We have celebrated, during this Year of Grace, all the grand Mysteries of the Redemption, and this ought to enable us to appreciate the glorious economy, as the Fathers love to call what we admire under another name. The spirit of the Church’s Liturgy at this close of her and our Year, lets us see the world, as though its end were come; it looks as though it were sinking away, down into some deep abyss,—and yet, no; it is only that it may shake off the wicked from its surface, and then, it will come up again blooming in light and love. All this has been the divine reality of the Year of Grace we have had put before us, yea, and in us, by our sweet Mother the Church; and now, we are, or ought to be, in a mood to feel a thrill of admiration at the mysterious, yet, at the same time, the strong and sweet ways of eternal Wisdom. At the beginning, when Man was first created, sin soon followed, breaking up the harmony of God’s beautiful world, and throwing man off the divine path where his Creator had placed him. Time and wickedness went on; till there was a family, on which God’s mercy fell; the light which beamed on that privileged favorite, only showed the plainer the thick darkness in which the rest of mankind was vegetating. The Gentiles, abandoned to their misery,—all the more terrible, because they had caused it, and loved it,—saw God’s favors all bestowed on Israel, while themselves were disregarded, and wished to be so. Even when the time came for original sin to be remedied, it seemed as though that was just the time for the final reprobation of the Gentiles,—for, the salvation that came down from heaven in the person of the Man-God, was seen to be exclusively directed towards the Jews and the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
.
But, the people that had been treated with so much predilection, and whose Fathers and first Rulers had so ardenly prayed for the coming of the Messias, was no longer up to the position made for it by the holy patriarchs and prophets. Its beautiful religion, founded as it was on desire and hope, was then nothing but a sterile expectancy, which kept it motionless, and unable to advance a single step towards its Redeemer. As to its Law, Israel then minded nothing but the latter, and, at last, turned it into a mummy of sectarian formalism. Now, while in spite of all this sinful apathy, it was mad with jealousy, pretending that no one else had any right to heaven’s favors,—the Gentiles, whose ever increasing misery urged him to go in search of some deliverer, found one, and recognized him in Jesus the Savior of the world; he was confident that this Jesus could cure him; so he took the bold initiative, went up to Him, and had the merit of being the first to be healed. True, our Lord had treated him with apparent disdain; but that had only had the effect of intensifying his humility, and humility has a power of making way anywhere, even into heaven itself.
.
Israel, therefore, was now made to wait. One of the Psalms he sang, ran thus: Ethiopia shall be the first to stretch out her hands to God. It is now the turn for Israel to recover, by the pangs of a long abandonment, the humility which had won the divine promises for his Fathers, the humility which alone could merit his seeing those promises fulfilled.
.
By this time, however, the world of salvation has made itself heard throughout all the nations, healing and saving all who desired the blessing. Jesus, Who had been delayed on the road, came at last to the house, towards which He first purposed to direct His sacred steps; He reached, at last the house of Juda, where the daughter of Sion was in a deep sleep; she is in it still! His almighty compassion drives away from the poor abandoned one the crowd of false teachers and lying prophets, who had sent her into that mortal sleep, by all the noise of their vain babbling: He casts forth forever from her house those insulters of His own divine self, who were quite resolved to keep the dead one dead. Taking the poor daughter by the hand, He restores her to life, and to all the charm of her first youth; proving thus, that her apparent death had been but a sleep, and that the long delay of dreary ages could never belie the word of God, which He had given to Abraham, his servant.
.
Now therefore, let this world of ours hold itself in readiness for its final transformation; for the tidings of the restoration of the daughter of Sion puts the last seal to the accomplishment of the prophecies. It remains now but for the graves to give back their dead. The valley of Josaphat is preparing for the great meeting of the nations; Mount Olivet is once more to have Jesus standing upon it, but, this time, as Lord and Judge!
.
Offertory
.
De profundis clamavi ad te, Domine: Domine, exaudi orationem meam: de profundis clavi ad te, Domine.
.
Out of the depths have I cried unto Thee, O Lord: Lord, hear my prayer: out of the depths have I cried unto Thee, O Lord!
.
The service we pay to God is, of itself, far beneath what His sovereign Majesty deserves; but the Sacrifice, which, every day, constitutes part of our service, ennobles it even to an infinite worth, and supplies all our own deficiencies of merit. This is what we are told in this Sunday’s Secret.
.
Secret
.
Pro nostræ servitutis augmento sacrificium tibi, Domine, laudis offerimus: ut, quod immeritis contulisti, propitius exequaris. Per Dominum.
.
We offer Thee, O Lord, this sacrifice of praise, as a repeated token of our homage; that Thou mayest mercifully accomplish in us, what Thou hast already granted, beyond our deserts. Through, &c.
.
The other Secrets, as in the Fourth Sunday After Pentecost.
.
Having, by these sacred Mysteries, entered into a participation of divine life, let us beseech our Lord, that we may no longer be subject to the dangers of this world. Let us say with the Church:
.
Communion
.
Amen dico vobis, quidquid orantes petitis, credite quia accipietis, et fiet vobis.
.
Amen I say unto you,—all things whatsoever ye ask for when ye pray, believe that ye shall receive, and it shall be done unto you.
.
Postcommunion
.
Quæsumus, omnipotens Deus: ut, quos divina tribuis participatione gaudere, humanis non sinas subjacere periculis. Per Dominum.
.
We beseech Thee, O almighty God, that Thou wouldst not permit to be subject to the dangers of this human life, those whom Thou hast admitted to the joyful participation of Thy divine life. Through, &c,.
.
The other Postcommunions, as in the Fourth Sunday After Pentecost.

DISPATCH · Wed, Nov 4, 2026

01 · A living world inside a cloud of silt. Sofia Crespo (@soficrespo91) and Feileacan McCormick, the duo behind Entangled Others (@entangledothers) and both keen divers, trained their own neural networks on footage from their dives to make Sediment Nodes (2022 to 2023), a generative video work in which murky water turns out to host algae, bacteria and small creatures that never existed. Minted on Ethereum and shown by the V&A (@V_and_A) and the Toledo Museum of Art (@ToledoMuseum), it comes to the East Slovak Gallery in Košice from Nov 9 to 30, part of EXTENDED, the gallery's platform for digital and new media art.

02 · Three chains, one museum. In Linz, the Francisco Carolinum (@ooeculture) is showing the collection it has built on the blockchain since 2021: more than 400 works by over 150 artists across Ethereum, Tezos and Bitcoin, from Larva Labs (@larvalabs) and Casey Reas (@REAS) to Rafaël Rozendaal (@newrafael) and LIA, curated by Julia Staudach, through Feb 7, 2027, with a twin presentation in Cryptovoxels. Among its latest additions is Beeple's (@beeple) EVERYDAYS: Late Stage Memetic Warfare, Day #6482. November brings an NFT workshop on the 13th, a catalogue launch for five years of the Digital Francisco Carolinum on the 19th and a livestreamed performance by Operator (@operator_______) on the 21st.

03 · Tell a phone your story and watch the walls change. On Nov 14 the Staten Island Museum (@SIMuseum) opens Anchoring Home by Stephanie Dinkins (@stephdink), an installation of video, sound and AI-generated imagery. Visitors speak into retrofitted telephones, and each voice flows through AI processes to reshape the images projected in the gallery, a generative document seeded with oral histories from the museum's collection, including the Black Angels of Sea View Hospital and residents of Sandy Ground. Dinkins was the inaugural winner of the LG Guggenheim Award (@Guggenheim) in 2023.

04 · New on https://t.co/hIfCL7iz9M: a head carved for a temple of beauty. Between 1911 and 1912 in Paris, Amedeo Modigliani cut Tête from a single block of limestone, one of a row of caryatids for a building he never made. Of his roughly 28 stone sculptures, most belong to museums, from MoMA (@MuseumModernArt) to Tate (@Tate). Never offered at auction and held in one collection for more than five decades, this one leads Phillips' (@phillipsauction) Modern & Contemporary Evening Sale in New York on Nov 17, estimated at $28 million to $35 million, the highest value sculpture Phillips has ever offered.

05 · And a history: in April 1965, Bell Labs (@BellLabs) researchers A. Michael Noll and Béla Julesz showed Computer Generated Pictures at the Howard Wise Gallery on West 57th Street, the earliest such show in the United States, two months after Georg Nees showed computer graphics in Stuttgart. The invitation was a small deck of IBM punch cards, visitors wore polarized glasses for the 3D works, and The New York Times (@nytimes) wrote that "the wave of the future crashes significantly at the Howard Wise Gallery." Not a single work sold.

text:
In the hours after the midterms, it is worth saying this plainly: Elon Musk is about to be hit with a fresh wave of concentrated hostility, and the rest of us who value what he is actually building should not pretend otherwise.

A man who was once treated as a progressive technological hero with electric cars, reusable rockets, and an open internet - has become, in the eyes of much of the left, an apostate. He bought Twitter and refused to keep the old speech rules. He ran DOGE and cut programs the left considered sacred. He warned, repeatedly and without euphemism, that demographic and institutional trends could lock in one party control. He put his own money behind the other side. For that, the hatred is now open and concentrated.

Starship is still the only credible path to making life multiplanetary. Starlink still connects people the old infrastructure never reached. Tesla still forced the entire auto industry to confront electric vehicles. Neuralink and xAI are still early attempts at expanding what a human mind and an artificial one can do together. The people who want to punish the man for his politics have not offered a substitute for the work. They have only offered the punishment.

Standing by him requires noticing the pattern. The same voices that once celebrated the green-car pioneer now treat the multiplanetary goal as a distraction or a vanity. The same institutions that spent years demanding more regulation of speech on private platforms now treat an open platform as the greater danger. The consistency is not in the principles; it is in the target. When a single person both builds the hardware of the future and refuses to stay inside the approved narrative, the response is not engagement. It is a campaign to make the cost of that refusal higher than the benefit of continuing.

The simple fact is that no one else is currently doing the combination of things Elon Musk is doing at the same scale, and probably never will. When the response is punishment instead of alternatives, the work that actually expands the frontier slows or stops.

I support Elon because the work matters more than the noise, and he is one of the few people who seems to genuinely want humanity to have a future. ♥️

text:
$SDHC Q3 2026 earnings: Smith Douglas sells more homes, but price cuts shrink profit

Smith Douglas Homes handed over more houses to buyers, but price cuts wiped out its profit growth. The entry-level homebuilder closed 5% more homes than a year ago, yet revenue barely moved at $263 million because average selling prices fell 5%. Chief executive Greg Bennett pointed to high mortgage rates and affordability pressures, which compressed gross margin to 16% and cut pretax profit by four-fifths.

• Home closing revenue: $𝟐𝟔𝟐.𝟓𝐌 (+0.2% from a year ago)
• Home closing gross margin: 𝟏𝟔.𝟑% (21.0% a year ago)
• Backlog homes: 𝟗𝟒𝟕 (+25% from a year ago)
• Diluted profit per share: $𝟎.𝟎𝟕 ($0.24 a year ago)

⚖️ 𝐕𝐞𝐫𝐝𝐢𝐜𝐭: 🔴 Bearish

The story got worse because building inventory drained cash and doubled the debt load while profit neared breakeven. Homes under construction rose 38% to 1,514, well above the 947 homes under contract, which pushed debt to $101 million and reduced cash to $6 million. One bright spot: a hiring freeze lowered overhead costs from last quarter, and new neighborhoods lifted the order backlog.

The question now is whether the 567 under-construction homes not in backlog will require deeper discounts to sell. Optimists see a growing neighborhood count ready to turn into cash handovers, while skeptics see unsold houses that will force another cut to gross margin. The fourth-quarter margin outlook on the conference call will settle it.

Full article with charts - link in bio

🐂 𝐁𝐮𝐥𝐥 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🟢 𝐍𝐞𝐰 𝐍𝐞𝐢𝐠𝐡𝐛𝐨𝐫𝐡𝐨𝐨𝐝𝐬 𝐊𝐞𝐞𝐩 𝐎𝐫𝐝𝐞𝐫𝐬 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐁𝐚𝐜𝐤𝐥𝐨𝐠 𝐆𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐢𝐧𝐠
Smith Douglas builds entry-level homes across the Southeast and Texas, and it is opening new neighborhoods to grow its volume. Active communities, the neighborhoods open for sales, rose 15% from a year ago to 113.

• Net new home orders: 777 homes, up 13% from a year ago
• Backlog — homes under contract not yet handed over: 947 homes, up 25%
• Southeast backlog: 622 homes, up 45% from a year ago
• Backlog contract value: $305.3 million, up 18% from a year ago

The larger footprint matters because it brings in more buyers even in a tough housing market. Because the builder cut average order prices by 6% to $317,000, the dollar value of its backlog grew slower than the number of homes.

What to watch: active community count at year-end. Reaching the 110 to 120 range management targeted earlier this year would show that municipal permitting delays have not slowed expansion.

🟢 𝐎𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐡𝐞𝐚𝐝 𝐂𝐨𝐬𝐭𝐬 𝐅𝐞𝐥𝐥 𝐅𝐫𝐨𝐦 𝐋𝐚𝐬𝐭 𝐐𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫
Management froze non-field hiring last quarter to protect profitability as home prices fell. In the third quarter, selling, general and administrative expenses — sales commissions and corporate overhead — dropped to $40.4 million from $41.9 million in the second quarter.

Other expense also swung from a $4.3 million charge last quarter to $0.2 million of income, because the second quarter's lot write-offs did not repeat at that scale. That cost discipline lifted pretax profit to $3.3 million from $1.9 million last quarter, even though revenue fell 4%.

What to watch: overhead costs in the fourth quarter. Another sequential drop would confirm the hiring freeze is offsetting the cost of opening new divisions in Texas and Alabama.

🐻 𝐁𝐞𝐚𝐫 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🔴🔴 𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐞 𝐂𝐮𝐭𝐬 𝐏𝐮𝐬𝐡𝐞𝐝 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐟𝐢𝐭 𝐍𝐞𝐚𝐫 𝐙𝐞𝐫𝐨
"Higher mortgage rates and affordability pressures have weighed on buyer demand and profitability," chief executive Greg Bennett said. To keep buyers signing contracts, the builder has cut prices and offered larger mortgage-rate subsidies.

• Average price of closed homes: $316,000, down 5% from $333,000 a year ago
• Home closing gross margin: 16.3%, down 4.7 percentage points from 21.0%
• Overhead costs: 15.4% of revenue, up 1.6 percentage points from 13.8%
• Pretax profit: $3.3 million, down 81% from $17.2 million a year ago

The direct cost of building and delivering homes rose 4.7 percentage points to 83.7% of revenue, while overhead took nearly all of the remaining 16.3% gross margin. That left operating profit at 0.9% of sales, down 6.3 percentage points from a year ago, so 5% more home handovers produced flat revenue and a 71% drop in profit per share to $0.07.

What to watch: the fourth-quarter gross margin outlook on the conference call. A number near 15% would leave the company at breakeven after overhead costs.

🔴🔴 𝐃𝐞𝐛𝐭 𝐃𝐨𝐮𝐛𝐥𝐞𝐝 𝐚𝐬 𝐔𝐧𝐬𝐨𝐥𝐝 𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐬𝐭𝐫𝐮𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐁𝐮𝐢𝐥𝐭 𝐔𝐩
Finance chief Russ Devendorf said the team stays focused on "preserving liquidity, managing inventory, and generating attractive returns on invested capital" during a weak market. Smith Douglas uses land options to avoid owning raw land, which is meant to keep debt low.

The balance sheet moved the other way this quarter. Homes under construction jumped 38% from a year ago to 1,514, which exceeded the 947 homes in backlog by 567 homes, up from a gap of 338 a year ago by our math. Real estate inventory rose 29% since December to $386.5 million.

Because the company built homes faster than it closed them, it used $33.3 million of operating cash in the quarter by our math. Notes payable more than doubled from $44.1 million in December to $101.4 million, while cash fell to $5.9 million.

What to watch: homes under construction relative to backlog at year-end. If unsold houses keep piling up, the builder will have to discount them to pay down its credit line.

🔴 𝐎𝐫𝐝𝐞𝐫 𝐆𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐭𝐡 𝐒𝐥𝐨𝐰𝐞𝐝 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐂𝐥𝐨𝐬𝐢𝐧𝐠𝐬 𝐁𝐚𝐫𝐞𝐥𝐲 𝐌𝐚𝐝𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐏𝐥𝐚𝐧
Bennett said the sales teams worked on "maintaining a steady absorption pace" — the number of homes each neighborhood sells per month. In the first half of 2026, net orders grew about 30% from a year ago and the builder closed 839 homes in the second quarter.

In the third quarter, net order growth slowed to 13%, or 777 homes. By our math, monthly sales per average neighborhood slipped to 2.3 from 3.0 last quarter and 2.4 a year ago. Home closings of 831 landed just six homes above the bottom of the 825 to 900 outlook range, breaking a streak of top-end finishes.

What to watch: fourth-quarter closings against the 947-home backlog. Closing fewer than 83% of beginning backlog would show that buyer financing delays are slowing handovers.

🔴 𝐑𝐢𝐬𝐤𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐪𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐝𝐢𝐝𝐧'𝐭 𝐚𝐧𝐬𝐰𝐞𝐫
Bennett said he expects "market conditions to remain challenging in the near term", and the earnings release left four standing risks without updated numbers because those disclosures live on the conference call or in the quarterly filing.

• Total buyer incentives: not in the release after reaching 7.8% of revenue last quarter; the call remarks will show if subsidies rose again.
• Land option write-offs: not broken out in the release against $140.6 million of option deposits; the quarterly filing will show any abandonments.
• Fourth-quarter outlook: Smith Douglas gives its quarterly targets on the call rather than in the release.
• Dual-class control and tax payouts: founders still hold 42.4 million Class B shares and a $9.4 million tax-benefit liability.

— • — • —

💲 𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐊𝐏𝐈𝐬

𝐂𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞𝐥𝐥𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐞 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): 𝟏𝟏.𝟑%  ⇘ decelerating
Buyer cancellations eased to 11.3% of gross orders from 12.7% last quarter, and sat almost even with the 11.2% rate a year ago. Lower cancellations after the 16.1% peak in late 2025 mean fewer finished homes fell back into inventory during the quarter.

𝐃𝐢𝐥𝐮𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐬𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐞 𝐜𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐭 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): 𝟖.𝟑𝟗 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
Class A diluted shares fell 7.4% from a year ago after heavy buybacks in the first half of 2026. As debt rose in the third quarter, the homebuilder slowed repurchases to 28,370 shares for $0.3 million, down from $4.4 million in the second quarter.

𝐓𝐨𝐭𝐚𝐥 𝐜𝐨𝐧𝐭𝐫𝐨𝐥𝐥𝐞𝐝 𝐥𝐨𝐭𝐬 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): 𝟐𝟒,𝟕𝟐𝟒 𝐥𝐨𝐭𝐬  ⇒ stable
The land pipeline grew 1.7% from a year ago and 5.1% from last quarter. The US builder holds 22,693 of those lots through options rather than direct ownership, which limits upfront land spending even as active construction on owned lots rose.

— • — • —

❓ 𝐊𝐞𝐲 𝐐𝐮𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬

𝐖𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐚𝐫𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐟𝐨𝐮𝐫𝐭𝐡-𝐪𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐭𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐞𝐭𝐬 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐜𝐥𝐨𝐬𝐢𝐧𝐠𝐬 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐠𝐫𝐨𝐬𝐬 𝐦𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐢𝐧?
Smith Douglas issues its quarterly outlook on its conference call rather than in the earnings release. With third-quarter gross margin at 16.3% and overhead at 15.4% of revenue, any further margin drop in the fourth quarter would push the business to breakeven.

𝐖𝐡𝐲 𝐝𝐢𝐝 𝐡𝐨𝐦𝐞𝐬 𝐮𝐧𝐝𝐞𝐫 𝐜𝐨𝐧𝐬𝐭𝐫𝐮𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐣𝐮𝐦𝐩 𝐭𝐨 𝟏,𝟓𝟏𝟒?
Homes under construction rose 38% from a year ago and outnumber the 947 homes in backlog by 567 units, by our math. Investors need to know how many of these houses are unsold speculative builds that may require deeper price cuts.

𝐇𝐨𝐰 𝐡𝐢𝐠𝐡 𝐝𝐢𝐝 𝐛𝐮𝐲𝐞𝐫 𝐢𝐧𝐜𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐢𝐯𝐞𝐬 𝐜𝐥𝐢𝐦𝐛 𝐢𝐧 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐫𝐝 𝐪𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫?
Subsidies for closing costs, price discounts and mortgage-rate buydowns reached 7.8% of revenue in the second quarter. Management previously said incentives in the backlog were even higher, and the conference call will show whether they have peaked.

𝐃𝐢𝐝 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐜𝐨𝐦𝐩𝐚𝐧𝐲 𝐭𝐚𝐤𝐞 𝐧𝐞𝐰 𝐥𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐢𝐦𝐩𝐚𝐢𝐫𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐜𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐞𝐬?
After booking $7.6 million of inventory write-offs and option abandonments in the second quarter, the builder holds $140.6 million of option deposits. The quarterly filing will show whether falling home prices triggered more write-offs.

text:
For nearly three days, an entire community in Kentucky was searching for one little boy.

Six-year-old Roman Heilman disappeared from Louisa on Sunday afternoon, November 1. He was last seen near Tadpole Road, and Kentucky State Police quickly issued an endangered child alert.

Roman has autism and is nonverbal, making the search especially urgent.

Hundreds of volunteers joined law enforcement and emergency crews. Search teams combed the surrounding area, while residents checked their properties, hoping to find even the smallest clue that could lead them to him.

Authorities shared one detail that could help: Roman responds to the children’s song “If You’re Happy and You Know It.” People were encouraged to sing it and clap their hands if they thought he might be nearby.

Then, on November 3, the news everyone had been praying for finally came.

Roman had been found safe.

Kentucky State Police confirmed that emergency crews located him in the Louisa area. He was taken for medical evaluation, and authorities thanked the local, state and federal agencies, along with the hundreds of volunteers who helped search for him.

The exact circumstances of where and how he was found have not been publicly released.

But after days of uncertainty, one thing mattered more than anything else: Roman was alive and no longer missing.

Imagine the relief his family must have felt after waiting through those terrifying hours.

This story is a reminder of what can happen when a community refuses to give up on a child. Strangers showed up, searched, offered help and kept hoping.

To every volunteer and first responder who helped bring Roman home: thank you.

Welcome home, Roman. May you recover safely, surrounded by love and care.

Last night was a sobering loss for Republicans. We owe voters an honest assessment of what happened—and the humility to listen. My read is that frustration over gas prices, the cost of housing, and the war in the Middle East weighed heavily. Families want affordable lives, security, and confidence in the future. We need to take their concerns seriously.

I believe these results reflect a pushback against the president and our party far more than an endorsement of the Democratic agenda here in Tennessee. But that distinction does not excuse us from examining our own shortcomings. We have to earn the public’s trust through both our conduct and our results.

For Republicans, the work ahead starts with getting back to basics: limited government, low taxes, free enterprise, public safety, and protecting family values. Those principles must translate into real improvements in people’s lives—good jobs, housing within reach, safe neighborhoods, and strong families supported by schools that prepare our children to succeed.

Our message must be about more than what we’re against. It must offer a hopeful, compelling vision of what we’re for and who we’re fighting for.

We should move forward with conviction, humility, and a willingness to work with anyone who wants to help our communities. The people we serve deserve leaders who listen carefully, speak respectfully, and deliver. That is where my focus will remain.🇺🇸🇺🇸

text:
The American people have spoken, including many who traditionally identify with the Republican Party but chose to cross party lines in this election. Beginning January 3, 2027, the responsibility and opportunity to lead will rest with the Democratic Party and those entrusted with representing us in Congress and the Senate.

As a Christian and an independent voter living in Texas, I sincerely pray that the years ahead will bring an improved quality of life, greater affordability, and renewed opportunities for all Americans, regardless of political affiliation.

I would offer one thought to those who might be hoping to see the Democratic Party fail over the next two years: perhaps we should all take a step back and consider what that failure could mean. When policies fail, the economy suffers, or hardships increase, the consequences rarely fall on just one political party. They are felt by families, working people, seniors, and communities across this entire nation. Ultimately, we all share in the outcome.

We may disagree on politics, policies, and the direction our country should take, but we should never lose sight of the fact that we are Americans first. Rather than wishing for one another's failure, let us hope and pray for one another's success.

My prayer is that our elected leaders will put people before politics, seek common ground where possible, govern with wisdom and compassion, and make decisions that benefit all Americans.

May we find a way to come together again as One Nation Under God, not simply for the betterment of our own country, but as an example of what is possible when people choose understanding over division, compassion over resentment, and unity over hostility.

We may not always agree, but we can always choose to wish one another well.

Peace and blessings to all.

text:
One of America’s favorite pastimes is claiming that election results vindicate our own political views. “The results prove that voters care deeply about the issues I champion and reject the positions I happen to oppose.”

We can all be tempted by that trap, so I try to focus more on exit polling than vibes. Here are my takeaways, based on hard evidence as much as possible.

1. Exit polling shows three things factored most for the Democratic wave: the economy/tariffs, corruption, and the Iranian conflict. Parties that come to power after a wave election often have trouble staying focused on the issues that swept them in. Can Dems in D.C. address those three issues first without distraction? We shall see.

2. The MAGA coalition is getting scrambled and it will be interesting to see what Republican coalition rebuilds in its place. Democrats won young white men tonight by 17 points, per CNN exits. Trump won them by *28 points* in 2024. That’s a massive swing.

3. Dems will get about 55 Senate seats and 250+ House seats. In light of the Senate map and the massive House margin, it is very unlikely Republicans will recapture the Congress in 2028. It may not be until 2032 the Republicans have a shot at retaking Senate control.

4. I’m struck by how Republicans controlled every branch of gov’t for last two years, but passed no major legislation. Just executive orders, all of which the next Dem president will rescind. Trump’s first term was consequential. His second might end up having the shortest-lasting policy legacy in modern history. 

5. Throughout nearly all of American history, Democrats and Republicans were equally religious. But over the last few decades that  began to change, with Dems decidedly less religious. Yet exit polls show Christians went from 6 points in favor of Rs to 4 points in favor of Dems. Democratic pastors or those who made faith central to their identity won big. Here are just a few examples winning to the Senate, House, or governor’s office: Hamilton (Kansas), Talarico (Texas), Garrity (Iowa), James (Iowa), Haynes (Texas), and Sands (Iowa). There’s a lot to unpack here with risks about drawing too strong conclusions from it. But my suspicion is that the increasing number of religious Dem candidates is more than coincidence.

6. I want to offer one final thought that isn’t based on polling. I strongly believe this election offers a lesson in hubris. The national GOP mistook one or two strong elections for a lasting political realignment. Yet this is the same electorate that returned Donald Trump to the White House just two years ago, after many had written his political obituary in the wake of January 6. Voter support is always conditional. Voters can reject one party without embracing the other. They can deliver a landslide without granting a blank check. And they can reverse course when those in power mistake a temporary victory for permanent loyalty.

No election should ever be taken as everlasting allegiance. They are judgments rendered at a particular moment, subject to revision when the evidence changes. The moment a political party forgets that distinction, it begins planting the seeds of its next defeat. Republicans forgot that, and if history is any guide, Democrats will forget it too. As voters, it’s our job to keep reminding them both.

text:
Here’s the rest of the story that most people in Western North Carolina/NC11 don’t know, but should. 

When Hurricane Helene hit Western North Carolina, Jason Simmons did not come to the region to lead the get-out-the-vote effort. He left that work to the District Chair. He assigned her not only NC-11 but the other Western North Carolina district as well.

While she was managing the numbers and helping secure special legislative measures so people in the mountains could vote, he was working to remove her.

President Trump visited Asheville. The stop at the airport was invitation-only. Some people were invited directly, and other invitations went through the District Chair. All of the allotted invitations were filled, and Merry Guy (current NC11 Chair from Henderson County) was not on the list. She and Joe still appeared. 

At that moment it was clear that Jason intended to replace Michele. He showed no interest in the solid results the district had produced, in her ability to pick up the phone and reach any legislator in Western North Carolina, or in her strong relationships with the press.

What mattered to him was that she had opposed Whatley and spoken out about Harvey West at least five years earlier—well before most people received a flyer in the mail. She warned the party. She warned Whatley personally.

Speaking the truth is not rewarded in this party. Those who do are treated as a problem. They can be pushed out, lose their jobs, or they will get some useful idiot to file lawsuits.￼

Merry Guy won the District Chair race on the strength of Henderson County votes. Older women using oxygen were brought into the room to vote. It was one of the ￼most unusual things I have ever seen.

In the last District Executive Committee meeting, members discussed spending district funds on a commercial against ROY COOPER! At the same time, a candidate had stepped forward to run for Chuck Edwards’ seat with fewer than 85 days until the election. The priority was not fundraising or advertising for that race.

The Henderson County GOP holds a war chest of approximately $60,000. They have not offered to spend any of it on ads for Jennifer Balkcom or Chelsea Walsh. The District has not asked the counties to pool resources to support the races. The money stays with the county party while the candidates are left to raise their own funds. That approach is reasonable under normal circumstances. It is not reasonable when candidates step in with fewer than 90 days to win. In those cases the response should be coordinated, collaborative, and focused on winning.

Instead, here we are.

Now we live with the consequences.

Elections have consequences.

Henderson is blue. 
The District Chair could not even protect the vote in her own county.

As Paul Harvey would say:
“Now you know the rest of the story.”

you must answer all these below questions:  

Agnipath gets a new pathway. Where is the review that justified it? Publish selection rules, costs, service benefits and outcomes. “Positive feedback” is not a public audit. Another chance is not guaranteed selection. 

Four years was the original model. Now the remaining 75% are offered another two years and a further chance at regular selection.

Which original assumptions changed?

What did the performance review actually find?

Why two extra years instead of higher retention after four?

What happens to those still not selected?

What happens to their original Seva Nidhi and accrued benefits?

Will earlier service count towards seniority or pension?

What is the additional cost—and what savings offset it?

How does the change affect future recruitment?

Who is accountable for delivery, and when will results be published?

Do not sell an opportunity as a guarantee. Do not call a policy change a proven success before showing the evidence.

Taxpayers deserve the cost comparison. Agniveers deserve clear written terms.

Publish the review, the rules and the measurable outcomes.

Questions the government must answer
A. Why change the policy?
What specific problem does the additional two-year engagement solve?

Was the original four-year exit model operationally unsuitable, financially inefficient, or less attractive to recruits than expected?

What evidence distinguishes those explanations?

When did the services first recommend a change?

Which alternatives were evaluated: higher retention after four years, longer initial tenure, or different arrangements by trade?

Why was a two-year extension preferred over those alternatives?

Was any pilot conducted? If not, what evidence substituted for it?

What assumptions in the original design have changed?

Which original objectives remain unchanged, and which have been revised?

What results would show that the revised policy is failing?

B. What does the performance evidence show?
What does “positive feedback” mean in measurable terms?

What were the assessment criteria, weightings and pass standards?

How did Agniveers compare with appropriately matched conventionally recruited personnel at similar experience levels?

What were training-completion, disciplinary, medical and voluntary-exit rates?

How did results differ across services, units and technical trades?

Did performance improve materially between years two and four?

What proportion of the original four years was spent in training rather than operational employment?

What evidence shows that retaining personnel for years five and six improves capability?

Who independently checked the evaluation?

Can aggregate findings be released without exposing operationally sensitive information?

Is every eligible member of the remaining 75% entitled to the extension, or can vacancies limit access?

Is accepting the extension entirely voluntary?

At year six, is selection based on a qualifying threshold, competitive ranking, or both?

Will there be a retention ceiling after six years?

Can someone meet the published standard but still be rejected because no vacancy exists?

Are standards uniform across the Army, Navy and Air Force?

How will medical conditions acquired during service affect eligibility?

How are performance records transferred when personnel change units?

What review or grievance process exists for disputed assessments?

When will recruits receive the final written rules?

Are approximately ₹43,500 in year five and ₹47,500 in year six gross monthly packages or take-home amounts?

What deductions and allowances apply?

Is the first four-year Seva Nidhi paid before the extension, deferred, or handled differently?

Are accrued first-term entitlements preserved regardless of the extension decision?

What exactly is the government’s second-term contribution formula?

Is it 70% of the Agniveer’s contribution, or a 70% share of a separate corpus?

What happens to the second-term corpus on regular enrolment versus voluntary exit?

Does any of the six-year Agniveer period count towards pensionable service, seniority or promotion?

Will those selected after six years face a different minimum regular-service commitment from those selected after four?

What insurance, disability and death benefits apply during the extension?

What is the additional annual cost under different extension-acceptance rates?

What are the lifetime costs under low, medium and high regular-retention scenarios?

What training or recruitment expenditure would the extension avoid?

What is the net cost per additional operationally deployable soldier-year?

Will extending existing cohorts reduce future recruitment?

How will the change affect force age, experience, promotion and vacancy profiles?

Can training establishments and units absorb the revised personnel pipeline?

How will early-retained and late-retained personnel progress without avoidable career bottlenecks?

Who owns implementation milestones and corrective action?

What aggregate expenditure, retention and outcome data will be published annually?

Canada’s message to Russia:

You cannot bomb Ukrainian cities and then send your junior players to compete in hockey in Alberta as if you were civilized people.

📍No Russian or Belarusian teams at the World Junior Championships. Not under your flag. Not under any other flag. Period. Canada has officially blocked the participation of Russian and Belarusian national teams in the World Junior Ice Hockey Championships, barring them from competing under any flag. This decision, supported by Hockey Canada and the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF), serves as a direct response to the ongoing military invasion of Ukraine. The stance reflects the principle that nations engaging in acts of war and the bombing of cities cannot participate in international sports competitions on equal footing with the civilized world.

Key facts and implications of the decision:

Total ban on participation: Russian and Belarusian hockey players have been barred from the tournament—precluding them from competing under either their national flag or a neutral banner (e.g., as independent athletes).   

📍Around 50 people may be buried under the rubble in Komyshuvakha.  Around 50 people may still be buried under the rubble in the town of Komyshuvakha in the Zaporizhzhia Oblast. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced the tragic news during a press conference in Berlin. The Russian army carried out a massive, repeated attack (so-called double-tap) using guided aerial bombs. The target was a former school, which served as a distribution point for humanitarian aid to local residents every Monday. When people took refuge in an underground shelter after the first strike, the Russians dropped further bombs directly on the site, causing the structure to collapse. Key facts about the disaster: • Death toll: At least 33 people have been confirmed dead, and the death toll continues to rise as work progresses. Among the dead were rescuers and police officers who arrived to help after the initial explosion. • Missing: Rescue services estimate that between 40 and nearly 50 people are still missing or trapped under the reinforced concrete remains of the building. • Challenging rescue operation: Work continues for a second day, but the operation is being severely hampered by thick smoke, damaged heavy firefighting equipment, and the constant threat of further airstrikes. President Zelenskyy described the raid as "one of the most horrific and largest Russian massacres of this war." He also emphasized the brutality of Moscow's intentions – the attack came just one day after the end of a local ceasefire in Oleshky, which was supposed to offer hope for de-escalation. Authorities in the Zaporizhzhia Oblast declared three days of national mourning.

They say history repeats if you don't learn from it. I guess we'll see.

Gleichschaltung (“coordination” or “synchronization”) was the process by which the Nazis brought all areas of German political, social, cultural, and economic life under the control of the Nazi Party and Hitler after he became Chancellor in January 1933. The goal was to eliminate pluralism, create a one-party state, and impose Nazi ideology and the Führerprinzip (leader principle) across society. 
https://t.co/uI8q7F0891

Key steps included:The Reichstag Fire Decree (February 28, 1933) and Enabling Act (March 23, 1933), which suspended civil liberties and allowed rule by decree.
Laws in March–April 1933 that “coordinated” the German states (Länder) by aligning their parliaments with the Reichstag election results and appointing Nazi-controlled Reich governors (Reichsstatthalter).
The Law for the Restoration of the Professional Civil Service (April 7, 1933), which purged Jews and political opponents from government jobs.
Dissolution or forced merger of trade unions into the Nazi German Labor Front (May 1933).
The Law Against the Formation of New Parties (July 14, 1933), which made the Nazi Party the only legal party.
Further centralization in 1934 that abolished the remaining autonomy of the states and created a unitary Reich.

By the mid-1930s, independent organizations (political parties, unions, professional associations, cultural groups, etc.) had been dissolved, taken over, or subordinated. Opposition was suppressed through a mix of legislation, propaganda, intimidation, and violence. This created the totalitarian framework that allowed later aggressive foreign policy without significant internal resistance. 
https://t.co/KQffAtFDLu

The Night of the Long Knives (German: Nacht der langen Messer; also called the Röhm Purge or Operation Hummingbird) was a violent purge carried out mainly on June 30–July 2, 1934. Hitler ordered the SS (under Heinrich Himmler) and Gestapo to murder the leadership of the SA (Sturmabteilung, or Brownshirts), led by Ernst Röhm, along with other perceived rivals and opponents. 
https://t.co/r4iMQVM8QR

Background and motives:The SA had been crucial for street violence that helped the Nazis rise to power, but by 1934 its size (millions of members) and Röhm’s ambitions threatened the regular German Army (Reichswehr), which Hitler needed for rearmament and legitimacy.
Röhm and some SA leaders wanted a more radical “second revolution,” including greater power for the SA over the military. Conservatives, the army leadership, and figures like Hermann Göring and Himmler pushed Hitler to act.
Hitler also used the opportunity to eliminate other enemies, including former Chancellor Kurt von Schleicher, Gregor Strasser (a former Nazi rival), and others.

Hitler flew to Munich and Bad Wiessee, where SA leaders had gathered, and ordered arrests and executions. Röhm was offered suicide and then shot. Nazi propaganda claimed it suppressed an imminent SA coup. Estimates of the death toll range from Hitler’s official figure of about 77–85 to higher modern estimates (often 150–200 or more, with some sources suggesting higher numbers including later killings). The purge solidified Hitler’s absolute power, reassured the army (which then accepted him), elevated the SS, and was followed weeks later by the death of President Hindenburg, after which Hitler merged the offices of Chancellor and President and took the title Führer. 
https://t.co/KQffAtFDLu

text:
Democracy is not a sacred human right. Over 2,400 years ago, Socrates warned it was a catastrophic structural flaw.

Socrates himself was sentenced to death by a democratic vote. 
So of course he did not appreciate democracy in a high regard. 
Socrates puts it like this:
Imagine a ship out at sea and they encounter storm ahead.
Who would you rather have in charge navigating through the storm?
A trained and experienced captain who understands navigation, wind patterns and ship mechanics? 
The sailors who are constantly bickering among themselves, never actually studied navigation, merely following captain orders. 
The ship owner who owns the ship but knows nothing about seafaring. 

The choice is obvious and requires no vote. Obviously the ship captain. 
So if we would never vote on who should navigate the ship through a storm, why would we assume every citizen regardless of wisdom, background and education is automatically qualified to navigate the state? 

Socrates crucial deduced that in modern democracy, voting is a skill, not a birthright. 
Like making music, healing people, commanding an army, requires skill. 
Socrates warned that “Birthright Democracy” (being able to vote just by being born a citizen) inevitably leads to collapse. 
Instead he advocates for “Intellectual Democracy” (voting by an educated and informed populace) 

In Plato’s Republic, Plato building on his teacher Socrates, illustrates the fatal flaw of democracy further with a brilliant parable:

Imagine an election between two candidates for public office, a Doctor and a Sweet Shop Owner.
The Sweet Shop Owner stands before the crowd and says:

"Look at what this doctor has done to you! He hurts you, gives you bitter potions, cuts into your flesh, and tells you that you can't eat or drink whatever you want. I, on the other hand, offer you sweets, wine, luxury, and immediate comfort!"

Then it was the doctors turn:

"I cause you pain and restrict your pleasures in order to cure your diseases and keep your body alive long enough to survive."

Socrates asks “How many voters in an uneducated crowd would vote for the Doctor?”

Democracy inevitably creates demagogues who win by promising immediate sweets instead of real statesman who prescribes bitter but necessary medicine who are cast out. 

So what’s the alternative? Surely not dictatorship. 
Plato proposed an alternative structure to defeat the demagogues:
Epistocracy and Philosopher Kings. 

Plato argued that a society should not be ruled by those who desire power or win popularity contests, but by those who have been thoroughly audited for wisdom, emotional sovereignty, and moral integrity.

Epistocracy (Rule by the Knowledgeable): A political model where the right to vote or govern is earned through demonstrated knowledge, civic literacy, and political competence, NOT granted automatically by age or birth. 

The Philosopher-King: Leaders who undergo decades of rigorous philosophical, mathematical, and practical training, living without personal wealth or private property, ensuring they govern purely for the collective good rather than personal enrichment.

You wouldn’t let an untrained civilians fly a plane, so you shouldn’t let an untrained electorate steer the direction of civilisations.

In modern society, we’ve built a democratic system where a vote casted by someone who spend his entire life studying politics and history holds the same exact weight as someone whose political views are sourced from 30 second TikTok reels. 

So should voting remain an absolute birthright? 
Or are we in a sinking ship?

text:
Canada 🇨🇦 is actually closer to the moderate, stable jurisdiction Elon has described wanting than many of the louder alternatives. The tax rates look high next to some U.S. states or certain resource jurisdictions, but they buy a durable balance: predictable rule of law, functioning institutions, social stability, skilled labour, and public infrastructure that doesn’t swing wildly with election cycles. That combination reduces long-term risk for capital-intensive projects even if the headline tax number is higher.

A Tesla Terafactory (or large-scale battery/vehicle manufacturing complex) in Alberta or Saskatchewan is realistic on the merits. Both provinces have abundant land, existing industrial and trades capacity from energy and mining, competitive provincial tax and royalty environments, and direct access to North American supply chains. The same logic supports a major launch complex on the Atlantic coast. Nova Scotia already has an active commercial spaceport project near Canso with over-ocean trajectories and growing federal and private backing; Newfoundland or Labrador offer similar low-density coastal corridors with even more room to expand.

The most interesting option is doing both in Labrador, anchored on Churchill Falls. The existing plant is already one of the largest hydroelectric stations in the world (roughly 5,400 MW), and major expansions (upgrades, a second powerhouse, and Gull Island) are now moving forward with provincial and federal involvement. That is clean, firm, industrial-scale baseload power in a place with vast land and minimal competing demand. An energy-hungry Terafactory and a Starbase-style spaceport could both sit on that power without the grid constraints that limit many other sites. Transmission and logistics would need real investment, but the resource foundation is already there and being expanded.

In short, Canada’s higher taxes are the visible cost of the stability and capacity that make large, multi-decade industrial and space projects feasible. Alberta/Saskatchewan for manufacturing, the Atlantic for launch, or Labrador for both, powered by Churchill Falls, are concrete ways that capacity could be used.

text:
EU tourism strategy targets a sector where around 99% of companies are SMEs

The European Commission’s Sustainable Tourism Strategy sets out a coordinated approach for an industry whose companies are around 99% small and medium-sized enterprises. That proportion identifies the scale of smaller firms within the sector, while the strategy’s proposed measures address business support, skills, data, transport and crisis coordination. The plan does not replace national tourism rules or frameworks with a common EU set of laws. Instead, it reflects that tourism is mainly managed by Member States, regions and municipalities, even as travel and tourism operate across borders. The Commission presents shared action as useful in that cross-border setting, while keeping responsibility distributed among the levels of government already involved.

The strategy’s business measures respond to difficulties identified among tourism SMEs, including shortages of workers and skills, fragmented activity and administrative burdens. The Commission also lists gaps in digitalisation and concerns about accessibility and affordability as challenges facing these firms. Its planned response includes simplifying rules and providing businesses with support for green and digital transitions. The strategy also proposes modernising VAT rules for travel and tourism, alongside those broader business measures. These are stated areas of action; the Commission’s announcement does not give a quantified estimate of how many firms each measure will reach or how large its effects will be.

The strategy proposes a Common European Tourism Data Space and an EU Tourism Observatory to examine trends across the sector. Together, the two planned structures give data collection and analysis a defined place in the EU approach. The Commission says they will be created to analyse sector trends, but the announcement does not supply a timetable, dataset size or particular findings. The observatory and data space are therefore described as future tools, rather than as sources of results already reported in the strategy announcement. This information work sits alongside the business measures, rather than changing the stated division of tourism responsibilities between EU and national or local authorities.

Skills are another part of the plan, with a new EU Tourism Academy intended to provide training in response to shortages in the sector. The identified skills problem is one of several pressures on tourism SMEs, which also face labour shortages, fragmentation and administrative burdens. The academy is presented as a training measure, not as a replacement for the business support or rule changes described elsewhere in the strategy. The announcement does not specify how many people will receive training, which courses will be offered or when the academy will begin operating. Its stated purpose is to address skills shortages in tourism, placing workforce development within the strategy’s proposed response to sector challenges.

Transport measures in the strategy cover rail, aviation, cross-border car rental and ticketing. The Commission says these measures are intended to improve connections for islands and for remote and coastal regions. Those places are specifically identified as beneficiaries of the connectivity work; the announcement does not provide route counts or a numerical estimate of improved access. The range of transport topics means the plan addresses more than one mode of travel and includes cross-border rental and ticketing arrangements. The stated purpose is better connectivity for the named areas, while the announcement does not quantify how travel patterns might change.

The strategy defines balanced tourism by whether visitor flows fit the capacity of a destination. That definition is concerned with avoiding disproportionate effects on infrastructure, the environment and local wellbeing. The Commission also aims to make fuller use of Europe’s tourism potential by encouraging travel across territories and during every part of the year. The stated emphasis is therefore on the distribution of visits across places and time, as well as on the capacity of destinations to receive visitors. The announcement gives no numerical visitor-flow threshold for balance, so its definition remains tied to destination capacity and the impacts named by the Commission.

For disruptions, the Commission proposes a Crisis Coordination Network to improve coordination during crises and inform tourists about their rights. The announcement identifies both coordination and tourist information as purposes of the network, without describing a specific crisis response or timetable. Implementation is assigned a separate collaborative structure: an EU Tourism Alliance involving the Commission, Member States, regions, local authorities and stakeholders. The alliance is intended to ensure that the strategy is carried out through cooperation among those participants. The network and alliance thus have distinct stated roles, one focused on crisis coordination and tourist rights information, the other on strategy implementation.

The strategy also extends the Commission’s international engagement through partnerships with Japan and India and a new cooperation framework with UN Tourism. These relationships are presented as international outreach, alongside the plan’s measures within Europe. The announcement names the partners and framework but does not set out specific joint projects, funding amounts or expected outcomes. Across the strategy, the Commission combines proposed business support, training, trend analysis, connectivity measures, crisis coordination and cooperation on implementation. Its wider premise is that tourism remains primarily within Member State, regional and municipal responsibility, while its cross-border character makes a shared EU approach beneficial.

The strategy’s scale is described through the composition of the industry rather than a target for visitor numbers: around 99% of EU tourism companies are SMEs. The Commission’s list of pressures on those firms includes labour and skills shortages, fragmentation, administrative burdens and digitalisation gaps, as well as concerns about access and affordability. Its response spans simpler rules, support for green and digital transitions, updated VAT rules, training and sector-trend analysis. Other measures address transport connections, crisis coordination, international relationships and cooperation among public authorities and stakeholders. Taken together, the announced approach seeks tourism across territories and throughout the year while defining balance through destination capacity and effects on infrastructure, the environment and local wellbeing.

text:
In 2016 a New York woman playing a penny slot machine hit a $43 million jackpot. The casino said the machine was broken and offered her a steak dinner.

She was 44, playing at Resorts World Casino in Queens. The screen lit up: "Printing cash ticket. $42,949,672.76."

She took a selfie with it. A crowd gathered. She called her mother and told her it was time to retire.

No ticket came out. Casino staff came over instead.

Then they told her the machine had malfunctioned. The state gaming commission checked its log and said she had actually won $2.25. That machine's top payout was $6,500. A small sign on it read: "Malfunction voids all pays and plays."

To make up for it, they offered her a free steak dinner. "I felt very robbed," she said.

She had to call her mother back. "It was totally hurtful," she said.

She hired a lawyer and sued for the full $43 million. "I feel like 43 million is worth fighting for."

A few years earlier, a 90-year-old woman in Iowa saw $41 million on a broken slot machine. The Iowa Supreme Court sided with the casino. She got nothing.

There is one more detail. The number on the screen, $42,949,672.76, is almost exactly 2 to the 32nd power in cents. That is the largest number a basic 32-bit counter can hold.

Her name is Katrina Bookman.

The machine said $43 million. The casino said $2.25 and a steak. Should they have paid her? Yes or no.

1SG, ARMOR WARRIOR DAILY ORDER
November 4, 2026 • Promise #308
FULLY KNOWN. WALK FAITHFULLY.

Today’s 365Promises statement: “I know everything about you and am mindful of all your ways.” This is the site’s promise paraphrase, anchored in Psalm 139:1–3. 

1 — THE ORDER
Receive His Word.

“O LORD, You have searched me and known me.”
— Psalm 139:1, NKJV. 

Read in context: Psalm 139, especially verses 1–6 and 23–24.

David addresses the Lord personally. God knows his ordinary movements, his thoughts, his activity, and his rest. Nothing about David’s life lies beyond God’s understanding.

Receive that truth with both comfort and humility. You do not need perfect words to bring your concerns before God. You also cannot hide a wrong attitude behind an outward appearance of discipline. The psalm ultimately turns God’s searching knowledge into a prayer: examine me and lead me.

Today’s order: Bring your actual condition before God. Receive His correction and take the next faithful step.

Battle Line: God knows me completely. I will walk honestly before Him and care for the person before me.

⸻

2 — THE TRAINING
Walk in His truth.

Warrior Doctrine — God’s knowledge invites honest dependence.

Begin prayer where you actually are: grateful, tired, concerned, impatient, or uncertain. Honest prayer gives you room to receive correction instead of defending your first reaction.

Armor Fit — The belt of truth, Ephesians 6:14.

Practice agreement between your confession and your conduct. If you need help, acknowledge it. If you spoke harshly, own it. If you have a responsibility, complete the next manageable part.

Training drill — Pause, name, respond.

Pause: Before answering a difficult moment, take one quiet breath.
Name: Tell God what is happening within you.
Respond: Choose one action consistent with His Word.

Cross-reference armory:

Hebrews 4:13–16: Being fully exposed before God leads into the invitation to approach His throne through Jesus.
Psalm 139:23–24: Ask God to examine your heart and guide your way.
James 1:19: Practice attentive listening and patience before speaking.

Spiritual Combat Medic: I belong to Christ, and I will care for the people He places in my path.

You cannot know another person as God does. Ask before assuming. Listen before advising. Give someone your undivided attention today.

⸻

3 — THE EXECUTION
Act, review, rest.

Commander’s Orders — Complete one deliberate act of attentive care.

Choose one person. Ask how they are doing, listen without rushing, and offer one practical kindness within your ability. Your measure of faithfulness is the care you give; their response belongs to them.

Morning prayer

Father, You know my thoughts, my concerns, and my ways. Help me come before You honestly. Correct what needs correction and guide my response today. Through Jesus, teach me to listen patiently and serve with love. Amen.

Evening after-action review

What did I learn about God today?
How did I respond when my heart was unsettled?
Did I listen carefully to someone?
What needs confession, repair, or attention tomorrow?
What mercy can I thank God for tonight?

Prayer of surrender

Father, thank You for knowing me throughout this day. Forgive my sins and help me make needed repairs. I entrust the unfinished concerns and the people I love to You. Give me rest in Christ and willingness to follow You tomorrow. Amen.
