$TLN KEY READ-THROUGHS FROM TALEN ENERGY’S Q3 2026 EARNINGS CALL

Talen’s call supports a selective infrastructure and power-market thesis rather than an indiscriminate “AI electricity demand” trade. The strongest positive implications favor existing dispatchable generation, transmission and substation infrastructure, and maintenance of the installed gas-turbine fleet. The strongest negative implications concern the assumption that physical power shortages necessarily translate into unrestricted merchant pricing, attractive returns on every proposed new power plant, or hyperscaler willingness to absorb unlimited electricity costs. Geography, existing contracts, and responsibility for infrastructure spending determine who captures the economic value. Several observations corroborate developments already reported by peers rather than creating new earnings surprises. The most actionable distinctions are therefore between operating assets and development pipelines, regulated investment and commodity exposure, and contracted cash flows and prospective scarcity premiums.

INDEPENDENT POWER AND COMPETITIVE ELECTRICITY

EXISTING GENERATION HAS A COST AND DELIVERY ADVANTAGE OVER GREENFIELD SUPPLY (READ-THROUGH 1)

Affected companies: Vistra Corp. (VST: United States), Constellation Energy Corporation (CEG: United States), and NRG Energy, Inc. (NRG: United States).

Directional impact and magnitude: Positive, potentially substantial for exposed PJM assets and moderate at the consolidated-company level. The immediate earnings sensitivity is considerably smaller than the underlying asset-value sensitivity where generation is already hedged or committed to customers.

Call evidence: Talen’s intermediate fleet capacity factor increased from approximately 36% to 52%, while 2028 AEP-Dayton Hub and PPL spark spreads increased 19% and 11%, respectively, during the quarter. Management also estimated that a new combined-cycle plant requires more than $120/MWh on an all-in generation basis. McFarland summarized the competitive position: “The demand is here, the supply isn’t and we already own the assets the market needs.”

Transmission mechanism: Existing plants can serve incremental demand without bearing the full construction cost, equipment lead time, permitting risk, and financing burden of new generation. Higher dispatch improves fixed-cost absorption, while stronger unhedged spark spreads increase contribution margin. Existing interconnections also become commercially valuable when customers prioritize delivery dates. This supports both the earnings capacity of operating assets and their negotiating position in long-term customer contracts.

Vistra has particularly relevant incremental exposure. Its October 30 Cogentrix acquisition added approximately 3.16 GW in PJM within the approximately 5.5 GW acquired portfolio, including the Patriot and Hamilton-Liberty combined-cycle plants in Pennsylvania. Talen’s commentary corroborates the strategic rationale for those assets. It does not establish a Q3 contribution from an acquisition completed in Q4. Constellation’s existing PJM generation and NRG’s enlarged Eastern generation portfolio benefit through the same operating-asset mechanism, although their customer obligations, hedges, and geographic mixes differ.

The key restraint is hedge coverage. Vistra’s August disclosure showed approximately 94% of expected 2027 generation and 72% of 2028 generation hedged, before the subsequently completed Cogentrix acquisition. Those percentages cannot automatically be applied to the enlarged portfolio, but they demonstrate why Talen’s market sensitivity should not be transferred directly to Vistra’s consolidated earnings. NRG’s retail supply obligations can also offset some benefits from higher wholesale prices.

Timing and catalysts: Near-term trading relevance centers on peer disclosures concerning plant availability, acquired-asset integration, and updated hedge books. The larger fundamental benefit accrues through 2027–2029 as contracts reprice and additional load becomes operational. Talen’s results support the value of existing capacity more strongly than they support an immediate, uniform upward revision to peer earnings.

CAPACITY REFORM LIMITS THE EQUITY VALUE OF UNCONSTRAINED SCARCITY PRICING (READ-THROUGH 2)

Affected companies: Vistra Corp. (VST: United States), Constellation Energy Corporation (CEG: United States), and NRG Energy, Inc. (NRG: United States).

Directional impact and magnitude: Negative for prospective uncontracted capacity upside and scarcity-based valuation premiums. Potentially material for longer-duration equity valuation, but limited immediate impact on already-cleared capacity revenues. NRG has a partial strategic offset through its ownership of CPower.

Call evidence: Management discussed the possibility of another capacity price cap for the spring auction and advocated a new compensated large-load demand-response product. McFarland argued that curtailment could provide “something that looks like a peaker or a battery.” Management also acknowledged a rationalization of load forecasts.

Transmission mechanism: Capacity demand depends on the accredited reliability requirement, not simply on announced data-center megawatts. Better-vetted load forecasts, qualifying customer curtailment, and additional supply procured through backstop mechanisms can reduce the residual capacity requirement. Price caps can separately restrict the compensation received for any remaining shortage. These mechanisms can lower expected future merchant revenues even while electricity consumption continues growing.

The important distinction is between a physical shortage and the shareholder’s entitlement to scarcity rents. Reliable generation can remain essential while market rules redistribute part of its economic value to customers, new entrants, or flexibility providers. Consequently, a bullish load forecast does not justify assuming simultaneously unrestricted capacity prices, maximum scarcity-hour energy margins, and no demand-side response.

This is not evidence that a new cap has already been imposed or that previously awarded revenues will be reduced. A cap extension can remove prospective upside without cutting earnings guidance that already assumes capped prices. Company-level exposure must be assessed by delivery year and revenue component; energy-hedging percentages do not establish capacity-revenue protection.

NRG’s January acquisition of CPower creates an offsetting opportunity to monetize flexible demand. However, Talen explicitly distinguished gigawatt-scale hyperscaler curtailment from conventional commercial and industrial aggregation. CPower’s existing platform is relevant capability, not proof that NRG will capture the proposed new product or that incremental earnings are already contracted.

Timing and catalysts: The December 2026 capacity auction, the framework for the May 2027 auction, and subsequent large-load demand-response rules are identifiable trading catalysts. The longer-duration implication is a lower justified premium for merchant earnings forecasts that depend on persistently extreme scarcity pricing.

REGULATED UTILITIES AND POWER DEVELOPMENT

PENNSYLVANIA AND OHIO LOAD GROWTH SUPPORTS NETWORK INVESTMENT, NOT AUTOMATIC WHOLESALE-POWER PROFITS (READ-THROUGH 3)

Affected companies: PPL Corporation (PPL: United States) and American Electric Power Company, Inc. (AEP: United States).

Directional impact and magnitude: Positive and potentially substantial for the multiyear regulated investment opportunity. The incremental information from Talen’s call is modest because both utilities have already disclosed significant customer commitments. Earnings realization remains dependent on ownership, tariff treatment, financing, and regulatory approval.

Call evidence: Talen cited approximately 31 GW of additional contracted large load in AEP territory and 10.7 GW in PPL territory by 2031, including approximately 6 GW of PPL data centers under construction. Management identified transmission investment and local load growth as the principal mechanisms for improving generation-zone basis.

Transmission mechanism: New substations, transmission connections, distribution facilities, and system reinforcements create investment opportunities for the utilities serving these customers. Where qualifying utility-owned investment enters rate base, the earnings mechanism is an allowed return on invested capital. Electricity sales and associated tariff revenues can contribute, but higher wholesale spark spreads do not flow directly into regulated utility profits.

The distinction is especially important for PPL. References to the “PPL zone” describe an electricity-market location, not ownership of Talen’s generating assets. PPL does not receive Talen’s merchant nuclear or gas-generation margin simply because prices improve in that zone.

The call also provides a useful geographic signal. Management acknowledged that Northern Virginia’s energized demand currently exceeds the visible operating load in Pennsylvania and Ohio, while arguing that construction in the latter markets is advancing. This supports an investment sequence in which network spending precedes full customer utilization. It does not establish that every announced project will reach its ultimate load.

PPL’s August disclosure already identified more than 11 GW under signed electric service agreements and more than 6.5 GW under construction. Those categories are not identical to Talen’s 2031 load forecast and should not be interpreted as a new commitment or a reduction in PPL’s pipeline. AEP had already announced its expanded capital plan on October 28, so Talen’s remarks principally corroborate customer demand rather than independently adding to AEP’s disclosed investment program.

The principal offset is cost allocation. Developer contributions, prepaid connection costs, and customer-owned infrastructure can reduce utility funding requirements but also reduce the portion earning a regulated return. Conversely, inadequately protected customer commitments can expose shareholders or existing ratepayers to stranded infrastructure. Customer credit support and minimum-demand obligations therefore matter as much as headline megawatts.

Timing and catalysts: Near-term catalysts are customer-agreement conversion, tariff approvals, financing updates, and project authorizations. The larger earnings opportunity extends through 2028–2031 as eligible investments enter service and customer load ramps.

EXISTING-PLANT CONTRACTING RAISES THE HURDLE FOR SPECULATIVE NEW GAS DEVELOPMENT (READ-THROUGH 4)

Affected company: PPL Corporation (PPL: United States), specifically its generation-development optionality rather than its core regulated network business.

Directional impact and magnitude: Negative for the assumed conversion rate and prospective returns of uncontracted new-generation projects. Potentially meaningful for development-option valuation, but limited immediate impact on established regulated earnings.

Call evidence: Talen estimated new combined-cycle economics above $120/MWh and emphasized that hyperscalers remain price-sensitive. Management favored combinations of existing generation, incremental capacity, storage, and potentially demand response as more economical alternatives. McFarland stated that powered land is principally a way to facilitate long-term capacity and energy contracts from the existing fleet.

Transmission mechanism: A customer seeking reliable power can compare a fully new gas plant with a package that combines existing generation and targeted reliability additions. If the latter offers a lower total cost or earlier delivery, the customer’s willingness to sign a sufficiently remunerative greenfield power contract declines. That can delay financial close, reduce project returns, or shift the required risk allocation toward developers.

PPL’s Invitium Energy development platform makes this a concrete company-level competitive issue. Its August presentation identified more than 5 GW of gas-turbine reservation agreements supporting potential projects, with PPL holding a 51% ownership interest. These are development opportunities and equipment reservations, not an operating fleet or a fully contracted earnings stream. PPL also stated that construction and material financial commitments would require signed energy supply agreements.

Talen’s approach competes for some of the same regional customer demand without necessarily requiring equivalent greenfield capital expenditure. The implication is not that PPL’s projects are uneconomic or will be canceled. It is that the full pipeline should not be capitalized at an assumed premium PPA margin before customer contracts establish the actual return.

This creates an important cross-portfolio distinction: the same data-center growth can be positive for PPL’s network investment while producing tougher competition for its generation-development platform. Demand growth does not guarantee equal returns across the electricity value chain.

Timing and catalysts: The actionable milestones are definitive energy supply agreements, final investment decisions, and conversion of equipment reservations into committed projects. The fundamental issue extends into the late-2020s and early-2030s rather than constituting a near-term regulated EPS downgrade.

GRID EQUIPMENT, CONSTRUCTION, AND TURBINE SERVICES

GRID-CONNECTED SOLUTIONS FAVOR TRANSMISSION AND SUBSTATION SPENDING EVEN WHEN GENERATION STRATEGIES CHANGE (READ-THROUGH 5)

Affected companies: Quanta Services, Inc. (PWR: United States) and Hubbell Incorporated (HUBB: United States).

Directional impact and magnitude: Positive, with moderate-to-high multiyear demand relevance to their exposed businesses. Talen’s specific opportunities are insufficient to quantify incremental consolidated earnings, and no supplier award was announced.

Call evidence: Talen described grid interconnection in 2028–2029 as a major customer priority and emphasized that grid-connected solutions provide superior long-run reliability and cost. Management also identified transmission upgrades as a necessary component of resolving regional congestion and supporting new load.

Transmission mechanism: Whether a data center ultimately buys nuclear power, contracts with an existing combined-cycle plant, adds storage, or incorporates demand response, a grid-connected configuration still requires electrical infrastructure. Transmission lines, substations, protection equipment, connectors, switching components, and construction services remain necessary. This makes selected grid suppliers less dependent on which generation technology wins the customer’s power contract.

Quanta participates through engineering, construction, installation, and related infrastructure services. Hubbell participates through grid hardware and electrical components. The earnings channels differ: Quanta needs awarded work, labor productivity, and successful execution; Hubbell needs product orders, manufacturing capacity, pricing, and delivery. Neither company earns revenue merely because a developer announces a gigawatt-scale campus.

The spending sequence is favorable relative to the ultimate load ramp. A site targeted for energization in 2028 or 2029 can require engineering, procurement, and construction substantially earlier. Supplier revenue and contractor work can therefore precede full data-center utilization, although project postponements can shift that timing.

The call is corroborative rather than an undisclosed booking event. Quanta had already reported Q3 results on October 29, while Hubbell’s October 27 release described continued demand and backlog growth in distribution, transmission, and substations. Talen’s comments support the durability of that demand, not an automatic upward revision to already-reported quarters.

Timing and catalysts: Near-term relevance lies in new awards, customer funding commitments, and evidence that delivery schedules remain intact. The longer-duration benefit is a broadening infrastructure workload through 2027–2030. No direct Quanta or Hubbell contract with Talen’s powered-land projects is established by the call.

HIGHER DISPATCH CREATES A MORE IMMEDIATE GAS-TURBINE SERVICE OPPORTUNITY THAN NEW-PLANT CONSTRUCTION (READ-THROUGH 6)

Affected company: GE Vernova Inc. (GEV: United States).

Directional impact and magnitude: Positive for Gas Power services, parts, and upgrades; modest at the consolidated-company level from Talen alone, but more meaningful if the utilization pattern persists across the installed fleet.

Call evidence: Talen’s intermediate fleet capacity factor increased from approximately 36% to 52%. Management described additional maintenance during September and October and discussed GE F-frame upgrades that can add incremental output. The call indicated that gas-fleet uprate opportunities amount to a few hundred megawatts or more across the portfolio.

Transmission mechanism: More operating hours and starts increase component consumption and can bring forward inspections, hot-gas-path work, replacement parts, and other maintenance under equipment-specific service intervals. Higher electricity margins also increase the economic value of incremental output, improving the return on turbine upgrades that can be completed during planned outages.

This is a different investment channel from the new-turbine backlog. Existing equipment can generate service and upgrade demand before a greenfield project is permitted, financed, built, and commissioned. The high replacement cost of new plants strengthens the incentive to maintain and improve installed units.

The supplier connection is narrower than a new project award. Talen explicitly discussed GE turbine technology and recurring upgrade offerings, establishing relevant installed-platform exposure. It did not disclose a new GE Vernova contract, a procurement value, or a final allocation of its development pipeline.

The revenue response is also not mechanically proportional to dispatch. Service agreements differ in payment schedules, maintenance coverage, and revenue recognition, while outages can be moved between periods. The defensible conclusion is stronger maintenance and upgrade demand, not a 44% increase in GE Vernova service revenue corresponding to Talen’s relative capacity-factor increase.

GE Vernova’s October 28 results had already described strength in Power services. Talen therefore supplies customer-side corroboration rather than a new quarterly earnings catalyst.

Timing and catalysts: Maintenance and parts demand can affect 2026–2028 execution, while larger uprates require engineering, customer authorization, and outage scheduling. This is a comparatively near-duration benefit within the broader power-investment cycle.

HYPERSCALERS AND AI INFRASTRUCTURE

AWS HAS A VERIFIED POWER-DELIVERY ADVANTAGE, WITH ACCELERATION REPRESENTING OPTIONALITY RATHER THAN COMMITTED CAPACITY (READ-THROUGH 7)

Affected company: https://t.co/SpqvHNV5fi, Inc. (AMZN: United States).

Directional impact and magnitude: Positive and substantial for the specific Pennsylvania campus’s development certainty; modest for AWS overall and small for near-term consolidated Amazon earnings based on the information disclosed.

Call evidence: Talen confirmed that the minimum AWS contractual commitment increases from the 480 MW level referenced for 2028 to 840 MW in 2029, a 360 MW or 75% increase. Management described construction progress favorably and indicated that an accelerated ramp could exceed the contractual schedule, potentially by several years. The financial outlook does not assume acceleration.

Transmission mechanism: Secured electricity supply removes an important constraint on converting data-center construction expenditure into operating capacity. A defined contractual ramp supports planning for buildings, electrical systems, cooling, and computing infrastructure. Faster power availability could bring forward revenue-generating capacity if the remaining facilities, equipment, and customer demand are ready.

Amazon is a confirmed customer, not an inferred beneficiary. The relationship provides a concrete example of an incumbent hyperscaler securing a large power position before the surrounding market becomes more constrained. That can be a competitive advantage against projects still seeking generation contracts or viable interconnections.

However, Talen’s forecast of approximately $2 per share of incremental cash flow from a 1-year acceleration is a Talen sensitivity, not an Amazon earnings estimate. It cannot be translated directly into AWS revenue or profit. Similarly, 840 MW of contracted electricity is not equivalent to 840 MW of incremental computing equipment; actual utilization and non-computing facility loads matter.

The minimum contractual ramp is already established and should not be treated as a new November order. The incremental positive information is the supplier’s observation that construction progress may permit earlier delivery. That remains an option until the relevant operating and contractual milestones are met.

Timing and catalysts: Near-term catalysts are disclosed energization milestones and a formally accelerated delivery schedule. The fundamental benefit is concentrated in 2028–2032 capacity availability. The call does not establish an incremental purchase order for any particular semiconductor or server supplier.

POWER AFFORDABILITY AND COST-ALLOCATION RULES CONSTRAIN HYPERSCALER PROJECT RETURNS (READ-THROUGH 8)

Affected companies: https://t.co/SpqvHNV5fi, Inc. (AMZN: United States), Microsoft Corporation (MSFT: United States), and Meta Platforms, Inc. (META: United States).

Directional impact and magnitude: Negative for incremental data-center project economics and the flexibility of future development plans. Potentially material at the campus level, but insufficient evidence for a quantified consolidated EPS reduction.

Call evidence: Management repeatedly rejected the assumption that hyperscalers will pay any electricity price. Terry Nutt stated, “The solution matters, but the cost also matters.” The call discussed new combined-cycle economics above $120/MWh, ratepayer-protection commitments, customer-funded additional capacity, and the possibility of scheduled curtailment.

Transmission mechanism: New data-center projects can face more than the commodity cost of electricity. Connection infrastructure, capacity obligations, reliability additions, and customer-specific cost allocation can increase the total cost of securing usable power. If these costs are borne by the hyperscaler rather than existing utility customers, they reduce project returns unless offset by better utilization, improved computing economics, or higher customer pricing.

The scale is economically meaningful. At a constant 1 GW electrical load, every $10/MWh of additional cost equals approximately $87.6 million annually. At 80% utilization, the equivalent is approximately $70.1 million. These are project sensitivities, not forecasts of any company’s actual electricity bill. Talen’s $120/MWh estimate is also a new-generation economic benchmark, not a disclosed AWS contract price or a complete delivered retail tariff.

Amazon is directly exposed through the Talen relationship. Microsoft and Meta are comparable large-load purchasers with established long-term power procurement strategies, including nuclear arrangements with Constellation and Vistra, respectively. They are not counterparties to a newly announced Talen transaction. Existing contracts can mitigate exposure where prices and obligations are fixed, but do not necessarily eliminate costs associated with future campuses or additional infrastructure.

Demand response introduces a further trade-off. Voluntary curtailment payments can lower net power costs or facilitate interconnection, but the customer must evaluate the opportunity cost of interrupting or relocating computing work. The relevant measure is the return on reliably available computing capacity, not simply the cheapest electricity contract.

Timing and catalysts: Near-term catalysts include large-load tariffs, cost-allocation rulings, and new power-contract disclosures. The more significant fundamental effect emerges as 2028–2031 projects move from development concepts to binding infrastructure and power obligations. The call supports scrutiny of incremental AI infrastructure returns, not a conclusion that AI demand is weakening.

NATURAL GAS AND APPALACHIAN ENERGY

HIGHER EXISTING-FLEET UTILIZATION SUPPORTS LOCAL GAS DEMAND BEFORE THE NEW-BUILD WAVE ARRIVES (READ-THROUGH 9)

Affected company: EQT Corporation (EQT: United States).

Directional impact and magnitude: Positive for Appalachian gas demand and potentially regional realizations; modest near-term

It's a shame that you and President Trump are only now recognizing what so many of us have been saying for a long time, especially after the midterms. Many of us were attacked simply for being the messengers, even though we were trying to warn you.

I like you, JD. I even watched your motorcade up close and personal when you visited the Smokies about a year ago. But if you're serious about a presidential bid in 2028, you need to listen to what people are telling you and act on it. You and Trump need to make these issues an immediate priority: putting America First, ending our involvement in unnecessary wars, addressing the economy, and putting American interests ahead of Israel's or any other foreign nation's.

This isn't just about Republicans who wanted a different direction for the party. It's also about the Independents who helped put you in office. You cannot afford to alienate us. Nobody wins without Independent voters. That's not rocket science, sir. It's simple math.

I voted for Trump three times, and I genuinely like you. But you've lost a great deal of my confidence this term. I'm not saying I voted Democrat in the midterms. I didn't. I held my nose and voted Republican. But I know plenty of people who did exactly what you're now acknowledging, and I understand why.

Here's another suggestion that I believe would go an unbelievably long way toward rebuilding trust: President Trump should offer a sincere, public apology to @RepThomasMassie. Massie has consistently been one of the most genuinely America First members of Congress, and he never deserved the treatment he received. I realize an apology might not come easily to Trump, but it would mean a tremendous amount to many of us, myself included.

And while you're at it, distance yourselves from Peter Thiel and the Palantir deal. The centralization of Americans' personal information and the potential for government surveillance should alarm every freedom-loving American. Decentralization protects liberty. Concentrating that much information and power in so few hands puts it at risk.

I'm saying all of this because I actually WANT you to succeed. But success in 2028 will require more than speeches, promises, and party loyalty. It will require listening to the people who helped elect you, acknowledging mistakes, and making meaningful changes.

America First needs to mean America First. Not Israel First. Not donors first. Not political insiders first. The American people FIRST.

text:
Got some info for you 👇🏻 

Here are practical Louisiana resources that can address overdue power bills, shut-off phones, and broader financial hardship for a disabled veteran. Availability depends on parish, income, utility provider, funding levels, and specific eligibility (e.g., honorable discharge, Louisiana residency). Gather key documents in advance: DD-214 or discharge papers, photo ID, proof of Louisiana residency, recent bills/disconnection notices, and household income proof.11
Military Family Assistance Fund (LDVA) This state program offers need-based grants of up to $10,000 in a 12-month period for housing, utilities, medical needs, and other essential expenses that create hardship. It is a strong match for power bills and basic bills. Applications require the documents listed above and are reviewed by a board (not same-day cash). Apply online via the LDVA site or contact the administrator (holly.talley@la.gov or 225.219.3700). Start by contacting a local parish Veterans Assistance Counselor.14
Utility bill help (power and related)
•LIHEAP (Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program): Provides heating/cooling assistance and crisis help for disconnection or pending shutoff. Crisis assistance is available year-round (subject to funding). Income limits are based on household size (e.g., roughly $30,618 for a 1-person household in recent figures). Apply through local community action agencies or parish providers listed on the Louisiana Housing Corporation site (https://t.co/SYYvMhTnm1). Bring a disconnect notice if applicable.17
•Entergy “The Power to Care” (if an Entergy customer): Emergency bill assistance targeted at elderly customers and people with disabilities who meet income guidelines (often 150–200% of federal poverty level). Funds come from donations and are distributed by local nonprofit partners. Contact 1-800-368-3749 or check the parish-specific agency list on Entergy’s site; local United Ways also administer related bill-credit programs in some areas.6 Other providers (CLECO, cooperatives, etc.) have similar funds such as Power of Sharing or Operation Round-Up. Call your utility’s customer service and ask about hardship or disability-related assistance. Deferred payment plans are often available directly from the utility.
Veteran-specific housing and utility support Supportive Services for Veteran Families (SSVF) programs (e.g., through Volunteers of America in certain parishes including Acadiana, Baton Rouge, Calcasieu, and others) can help with utility arrears, deposits, and prevention of homelessness. Contact local SSVF providers or call the National Call Center for Homeless Veterans (1-877-424-3838) if housing is at risk.8
Phone service The federal Lifeline program offers discounted or low-cost phone (or broadband) service for qualifying low-income households. Eligibility is typically based on participation in programs like Medicaid, SNAP, SSI, or Veterans Pension, or household income at or below 135% of federal poverty guidelines. Multiple providers operate in Louisiana (search “Lifeline Louisiana” or check the National Verifier). This can help restore or replace shut-off service; one benefit per household.53
Additional steps Contact the Louisiana Department of Veterans Affairs (LDVA) first for free help maximizing federal VA disability compensation, pensions, and state benefits—there is a Veterans Assistance Counselor in every parish (locator on https://t.co/P00bVM9h1q or call 225.219.5000). Higher disability ratings unlock property-tax exemptions and other state benefits that free up money long-term. Dial 211 statewide for local referrals to food, utility, and emergency aid. If in crisis, use the Veterans Crisis Line (988, then 1).11
These programs are designed for exactly the situations described. Official applications through LDVA, local agencies, or utility partners are the most reliable path; funding can be limited, so apply promptly with complete documentation.

Washington State 

AMAZON WORLD

Amazon plans its first data centers in Washington State as residents raise concerns

Nov. 4, 2026

Amazon is moving toward building its first data centers in Washington state, with a proposed campus in Walla Walla County and a second in the Tri-Cities that the company confirmed this week.

The expansion into Amazon’s home state comes amid nationwide pushback against the rapid deployment of new AI data centers. Tuesday’s election underscored the scrutiny facing data center developers, with voters in communities across several states backing limits on new projects. In Eastern Washington, the Amazon proposals have drawn calls for greater environmental oversight and a temporary halt to data center development.

Amazon already has a substantial footprint in neighboring Oregon, where industry tracker Baxtel lists 64 AWS data center sites. Expansion there has divided communities, with residents pushing for restrictions over power and water concerns while some Eastern Oregon officials warn that slowing development would jeopardize jobs and tax revenue.

Both proposed Washington campuses would initially include three data center buildings. The Walla Walla County site covers roughly 134 acres in Wallula Gap, while the Tri-Cities campus is on a 1,000 acre property in the city of West Richland and could eventually grow to 21 buildings.

The Tri-City Herald first reported Monday that Amazon was behind the West Richland project. The company plans to hold a community open house Nov. 19 to discuss the proposal.

A full build-out of the West Richland campus could create more than 1,000 full-time data center jobs, Amazon said. Dallas real estate firm Trammell Crow initially purchased the property from the estate of agricultural businessman Frank Tiegs, who died in 2024, before selling it to Amazon.

Nearby residents have raised concerns about the planned campus, in part because of its proximity to about 200 homes. Residents asked the local city council to approve a temporary moratorium, but at a meeting Tuesday evening, council members adopted rules that removed a data center noise exemption, banned them in light industrial zones, and prohibited cryptocurrency mining. The council failed to pass a moratorium, NonStop Local reported.

Amazon says the upcoming open house will give residents an opportunity to ask questions about the planned development. A spokesperson described a “science fair” format, with booths hosted by experts discussing water and energy usage, job creation, noise and environmental impacts.

“We’re committed to growing responsibly and we want the community to leave the Open House with a better understanding of this project and what it could mean for the area,” the spokesperson said via email.

Calling for increased oversight
At Wallula Gap, a recent public-comment period offers an indication of the scrutiny Amazon faces.

Of the 706 submissions received during a 30-day comment period that closed Oct. 12, only 23 — about 3% — supported the project, according to an analysis by the Walla Walla Union-Bulletin. Most of the supportive comments came from the area, and many predicated their support on more stringent oversight of the proposed facility near the Columbia River.

More than 500 submissions came from outside Walla Walla County, according to the Union-Bulletin. Many included template language calling for an Environmental Impact Statement — a higher level of environmental assessment than currently required for the campus.

The proposed facility is located at the Wallula Gap Business Park, on property formerly owned by the Port of Walla Walla. The three proposed single-story data center buildings would create approximately 120 to 150 full-time jobs, Amazon said.
